Sports.title: Jose Mourinho goes on bizarre Vinicius Jr and Kylian Mbappe rant as he compares Real Madrid stars to FRUIT TREES
Sports.content:
JOSE MOURINHO went on a bizarre rant in which he compared Vinicius Jr and Kylian Mbappe to FRUIT TREES.

The Real Madrid stars were booed by their own fans this week following the defeat to Real Betis on Friday.



The team responded with a 2-1 win over Inter Milan in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

During the match, Mbappe and Vinicius were jeered by the Bernabeu crowd.



They had been criticised for their lack of contribution to the defensive side of the team’s performances.

It has also been suggested that fans were still unhappy with the club’s failure to win a single trophy last season.



Mbappe responded with the opening goal against the Italian outfit before Federico Valverde netted the hosts’ second.

Mourinho has now defended the pair and insisted that those criticising are only trying to “get a piece” of them.

He said: “In Portuguese, we have a proverb that says we only throw stones at the trees that have fruit.

“So what Vini has done here over recent years – how many CL has he won, how many goals has he scored, how many balls has he won?



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“His achievements speak for themselves so he is the tree that has a lot of fruit on it and people want to get a piece of Vini.

“During this digital era where we have access to so many stats, we can tell that he is very close to getting to his best version.

“He’s even set some records already.

“The stats and numbers he registers suggest we will see his best version very soon.”

Mourinho continued his rant and further claimed that Mbappe is not “a problem” due to his goalscoring exploits.



He added: “I want to remind you of the proverb I said before. He is the tree with a lot of fruit.

“Obviously, a player who scores more than 40 goals for a team is never a problem.

“I saw Kylian giving it his all. He was defending like an animal, even when he had nothing left.

“His attitude is incredible. It is a joy for me to see a player like that.”

Real are currently 4th in LaLiga after four games in which they have won three and lost once.

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal kid Dan Ballard is the Sunderland ‘warrior’ ready-made to take over from Granit Xhaka
Sports.content:
DAN BALLARD left Arsenal a boy. Now he is the “warrior” Sunderland’s top brass are most proud of.

The all-action defender, 26, may not be captain on Wearside. He does not need it. A more natural leader you will not find.



And once skipper Granit Xhaka is eventually ready to hand over the armband, they already have a tailor-made candidate to take over the club’s march to the big time.

It was Ballard’s winner in stoppage time of extra time against Coventry City in the Championship play-off semi-final in 2025 that ultimately set them up for Wembley glory against Sheffield United.



There was no stopping the Northern Ireland international in the Premier League either. A goal in an opening day victory over West Ham set the tone for a fairytale campaign.

The club may have splashed the cash on stars such as Malick Fofana and Dayann Methalie since. But there is nobody Sunderland would rather have in the heart of their side as they prepare for a European adventure 53 years in the making.

Sporting director Florent Ghisolfi, who recently tied Ballard down to a new contract until 2029, told Sun Sport: “Dan is not something normal. He played so much in the Championship and then when you see him today he’s just a top player. He’s a warrior.

“They are the most important players in the team because they are the legacy.

“We’ve spoken about the balance between leadership and young potential, but this balance between new players and legacy is also very important.

“We are proud to help this type of player to be a player who plays Premier League and Europa League.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Ballard arrived at Stadium of Light after they had finally managed to escape League One wilderness. He cost around £1m from Arsenal and has proven to be one of the best bargains in the club’s history.

The tough centre-back’s impact has not just been felt on the pitch. His presence is felt right the way through the club’s Academy of Light HQ.

Academy graduate Chris Rigg, 19, has been alongside Ballard throughout Sunderland’s incredible rise.

He told The Sun: “He’s such a good lad. He comes across as this big guy, but he’s really soft, really.



“He’s an outstanding footballer. He’s come through the leagues and showed what he can do. He’s a really important part of our group on and off the pitch.”

Ballard has undergone quite the transformation from the first time he stepped into the Academy of Light a decade ago.

Ballard had just been told he was getting released for a second time, the first coming when he was a midfielder aged 14. Despite that and nursing a back problem, the then 16-year-old accepted an invitation to take a three hour train from London to play for Arsenal’s academy against his current employers.



He knew he needed to play in order to impress any watching scouts, only the pain from his injury forced him off.

Ballard left believing his shot at the big time was done. But his guts and talent did not go unnoticed. He finally managed to earn a scholarship deal after receiving another bite of the cherry with Arsenal and eventually turned pro.

After loans at Swindon Town, Blackpool, and Millwall, Arsenal sold Ballard permanently to Sunderland without him making a senior competitive appearance at the Emirates.



Leaving a club after 15 years would be daunting for anybody. But it was a move that proved to be the making of him. And he finally got his coming of age moment last November.

After thundering in a strike in a draw against eventual champions Arsenal, he flexed his muscles in celebration in front of his adoring Mackem public.

Another iconic image to add to the collection in the red and white.

Ballard’s legendary status up north is already secured. But another Black Cats icon reckons he is ready-made to take over from Xhaka one day.

And the centre-back has been backed to kick off the club’s biggest week for over half a century by writing another chapter in his Sunderland love story against his old club today.



Speaking to Sun Sport via BestBettingSites, former striker Kevin Phillips said: “Xhaka is more of a household name but Ballard has been outstanding at Sunderland.

“He reminds me probably of a guy called Jody Craddock, who signed on the same day with me at Sunderland, a no-nonsense centre-half.

“The fans loved him because he loved a battle, he loved to get stuck in, and he chipped in with a few goals.

“Ballard has got a big future in front of him. If he could emulate what Xhaka has done in his career, then wow, he’ll go on to be some player.

“He definitely steps up on the big occasions, and it wouldn’t surprise me if he does it again at the weekend.”

Sports.title: Premier League clubs are frustrated to be left in the dark over Man City charges – and it could cost them £100m
Sports.content:
THERE is one subject which makes Premier League executives suddenly become very, very careful with their words — Manchester City.

Ask a chief executive what they think of the 130 financial breaches brought against City and you get the same answer: “I can’t comment.”



Ask when they think the verdict will come: “I can’t comment.”

It is almost as if somebody has handed every Prem chief executive the same script. But privately, of course, people talk.



The biggest frustration among the other 19 clubs is not simply that the case has taken so long, or it has cost so much money.

It is that they have almost no idea what is actually happening.

The Premier League have published the charges. But the evidence behind them is not public. Nor is City’s detailed defence.

So the clubs are effectively being asked to wait patiently for a verdict in a case whose workings they cannot see.

Football hates a vacuum. When there is no information, speculation takes over.

The Premier League formally announced the charges in February 2023, after a four-year probe.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Is the case taking so long because the evidence is so complicated? Are the three members of the independent commission divided?

Have they reached conclusions on some charges but not others?

Or have they actually reached a verdict and are simply taking enormous care to make the judgment legally watertight so that it cannot be challenged?

Nobody outside that room knows.

And that, ironically, is why there is so much speculation.



The allegations are hardly trivial.

At their heart is the Prem’s claim City deliberately misrepresented aspects of their finances and remuneration, potentially allowing them to comply with financial rules when, the League says, they should not have.

There are allegations concerning sponsorship income, remuneration connected to Roberto Mancini through an Abu Dhabi company, and player image-rights deals.

City deny wrongdoing and are entitled to defend themselves.

Now Mauricio Pochettino has raised another uncomfortable question, saying Tottenham should be awarded the 2017 title after Chelsea were punished for historic breaches involving agent payments.



I understand his argument. If clubs break the rules, there has to be a consequence. Otherwise rules are little more than suggestions. But I am not convinced you can simply hand the title to the team finishing second.

Football is not a school exam where you disqualify the winner and automatically give the prize to the runner-up. Spurs finished seven points behind Chelsea.

You would have to establish not only that Chelsea broke rules but that the breach justified removing the title and that Spurs should inherit it. That is a high bar.

What Pochettino is absolutely right about, though, is that punishment has to mean something.

A fine, however large, can look rather different to a football club than a sporting sanction.



And that brings us back to City. If the allegations are ultimately proven, the question is not simply: How much should they pay?

It will be: What sporting consequence, if any, properly reflects what happened? That is why this case matters so much.

I am not suggesting for a second that an independent commission should rush a decision simply because football is impatient. But patience has a funny quality when you are the person paying for it — and the other clubs have been paying.



They have already spent tens of millions. If City win, the other clubs will have to pick up their legal bill, estimated to be around £100million. Then comes another extraordinary detail. When the decision is reached, the Prem board and City will know the verdict three days before it is made public.

City know. The Prem board knows. Everyone else waits.

And still, officially, the answer is: “I can’t comment.”

Perhaps that is right. But when people are denied information, they start guessing.

That is why I suspect the other clubs are less interested in some grand conspiracy than they are in something much more mundane.



They want to know what is taking so long. They want to know what they are paying for and when it will end.

If City are cleared, football needs to accept it. If found guilty, football needs to accept that too, and deal with the consequences.

But after all these years, all the charges and tens of millions spent in legal costs, the Prem is entitled to expect its independent process to reach the finishing line.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Not because City deserve to lose or because the other clubs deserve to win. Simply because eventually, even in football, there has to be an answer.

Right now, there isn’t.

Sports.title: Richarlison transfer exit ‘COLLAPSES’ after he tried to have Spurs contract ripped up – as De Zerbi takes brutal swipe
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM striker Richarlison has seen a transfer to Brazilian side Vasco de Gama collapse in the latest set-back for the wantaway star.

The ex-Everton man, 29, was left out of Roberto De Zerbi‘s Premier League squad after requesting to leave but turned down a return to his old club.



After a move to Turkish side Trabzonspor also fell apart, he turned his attentions to Vasco with Brazil’s transfer deadline closing at 4am on Saturday morning.

But it’s understood Richarlison failed to agreed personal terms and will now stay with Tottenham.



Richarlison is exploring whether he has a case to terminate his contract as he looked to force his way out of Spurs.

SunSport understands Richarlison would face a serious fight to have any case attempting to prove “sporting just cause” for contract termination upheld by Fifa now.



That is because even if his lawyers managed to prove sporting just cause, it would have to be done during a 15-day window AFTER the club’s final official match at the end of the season.

Richarlison was pictured in first-team training on Tuesday but cannot feature against Everton on Saturday.

Asked if the forward was close to a move or likely to stay now, an exasperated De Zerbi replied: “I don’t know, I don’t know. It’s not my job.

“What I can say is I know very well what the club has done for Richarlison and I know very well what the Richarlison has done for the club in the last month, two months.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“I know, the club knows, he knows, his agent knows, everyone knows. Better than you (the media). Much better.”

Meanwhile, De Zerbi has branded Mykhailo Mudryk’s ankle injury as “stupid”.

The Ukrainian is out for six to eight weeks with the problem, having only just returned to action following 20 months out for a doping ban which has since been resolved.

Mudryk, who signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, made his Spurs debut as a late sub in Saturday’s 0-0 draw at Nottingham Forest but will now be out for the forseeable.

De Zerbi said: “Mudryk, it was a stupid injury and we hope he can come back as soon as possible.



“For him and for us. For him because he suffered too much and for us because we lost an important player.

“He played 15 minutes in Nottingham, he played well. But it’s in the normal process when one player doesn’t play for a long time.”

Asked to clarify what he meant by “stupid”, De Zerbi replied: “Playing without taking different movements, he felt pain in his ankle.

“Then after two days, he made the medical check and we knew the problem.

“It’s a stupid injury, but we are nots stupid. When we signed Mudryk we already knew it could be difficult to come back as a normal player.”

Sports.title: Former Sky Sports reporter and Ronnie O’Sullivan’s ex reveals why she’ll NEVER work in football again
Sports.content:
FORMER Sky Sports reporter Bianca Westwood has claimed she will “probably” never work in football again.

The 51-year-old took a voluntary redundancy from Sky in 2023 after 22 years with the broadcaster.



Westwood became popular with fans after making a name for herself as a pitchside reporter during their hit Soccer Saturday show.

But now she has started a new career venture posting about fashion and beauty on social media.



And Westwood – who dated Snooker legend Ronnie O’Sullivan in the early 2000s – explained why she is leaning towards a future as an influencer rather than returning to football.

She said in a TiKTok video: “I wanted to set a few things straight because I still get a lot of messages asking about Sky.

“When am I going back to Sky? When am I doing the football again? The compliments are really nice, I do appreciate them, but I’m not going back to Sky.

“It’s funny because I get so many compliments now about what a good reporter I was, which is lovely, how I was the best football presenter, blah, blah, blah… and yet when I was doing it, especially when I first started, everyone said I was s***. So, work that out.

“The thing is, I’m not going back to Sky and I’m probably never going to work in football again.

“I had a feeling, probably about a year before I left Sky that the opportunities were becoming few and far between, they didn’t really rate me, that’s why I started doing the fashion, beauty and skincare, things that I love as a woman.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“All my content now is geared towards women so I don’t even know why I get new male followers because the football has gone.

“I love what I do now so I just wanted to let you know what that’s all about.

“Three years ago, Sky offered me redundancy, I decided to take it. Jeff [Stelling] was leaving at the same time, I thought it was probably the best time to go and that was basically the reasons behind my decision so I’m not really going to go back.”



Westwood first started dating O’Sullivan in the summer of 2000 and she famously watched his first World Snooker Championship title win.

Their romance was short lived as they ended up splitting one year later in 2001.

Westwood was an iconic part of Soccer Saturday alongside usual favourites like Matt Le Tissier, Phil Thompson and Charlie Nicholas, who all left the show in 2020.

Host Jeff Stelling initially stayed on before following them out the door in 2023 – the same year Westwood departed.

Westwood – who has 138,000 followers on Instagram and 45,000 on TikTok – joined Sky in 2000 as a runner before later becoming a sports reporter for Sky Sports News.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta sends warning to Arsenal's Premier League title rivals as secret target set
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta sends warning to Arsenal's Premier League title rivals as secret target set

Arsenal have enjoyed a brilliant start to their title defence with the Gunners catching the eye with some of their recent performances under Mikel Arteta this term

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta takes his Arsenal side to Sunderland this weekend (Image: Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta is enjoying Arsenal being the great entertainers - but insists they can get even better. The reigning champions have started the season in real style with three straight wins in the Premier League and they have played free-flowing football.

Arsenal were christened Set Piece FC last season because they were so good at scoring from corners and free kicks but all of their goals this term have been from open play.

Arteta says that is down to having the likes of Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz back to form and full fitness but he has set a target to play with more “flair” this season.

They face Sunderland on Saturday night on the back of an impressive Champions League win at Napoli when they dominated but only had Odegaard’s goal to show for their dominance.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Gunners boss Arteta says he wants his players to be more efficient and ruthless with their finishing as they look to defend their title. Arteta, whose side travel to Sunderland on Saturday night, said: “I like a lot what I’ve seen from the team so far.

“For sure, it’s for flair but also just making sure what happens on the pitch is what we want. And having that dominance and control and threat in our minds.

“It’s the way we have to continue and evolve in certain areas and that is an area that we have put a lot of emphasis into and now we have a lot of players back.

“The opportunities and synergies that we create with the team are much stronger and we’re going to continue to be like that. That’s always the intention.

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta is aiming to claim back-to-back Premier League titles this season (Image: Getty Images)

“Sometimes it’s the level of the opponents, sometimes the level of execution and that has to increase as well to be much more efficient and dominant throughout the games and we will continue to do that.”

Arteta has been fulsome in his praise for captain Odegaard who looks back to form, fitness and sharpness after an injury-plagued couple of seasons.

Odegaard scored the winner at Chelsea last Sunday, again at Napoli in the Champions League in midweek and Arteta also says Havertz’s return has also been key.

Arteta says Havertz’s intelligence means he is ahead of everyone else on the pitch and therefore it is difficult to pin down his best position.

View 3 Images Kai Havertz has had a bright start to the season (Image: Getty Images)

Arteta said: “The best position is in relation to what the game demands and what the team demands on the day. To be as efficient as possible, as unpredictable as possible. Kai is extremely intelligent, that's his biggest quality.

“He understands the game, he's five, ten seconds ahead of the game, he knows what he's having, he doesn't need to think about it, he just acts. And he just makes the people around him better, which is another massive quality.

“On top of that, he's scoring goals, he's producing chances, his work rate, as we all know, is just outstanding. And he's in a great emotional state at the moment.”

Arteta also praised the impact of one of the club’s new summer signings as Ezri Konsa - who joined in a £55m deal from Aston Villa - has looked at home immediately.

Arsenal were held to a 2-2 draw at Sunderland last season and their back four is certain to be tested again with Arteta insisting Konsa’s personality and defensive abilities have been key.

Arteta added: “Well, it's certainly something to admire because it's not easy at all and you should not take it for granted. But after talking to a lot of people that have worked with him, whether staff members or players, I already had a sense the way everybody was talking about him.

“That he's a person that is great at gathering people together. He has a real personality, a lot of leadership skills.

“And you saw the first day, he just trained the way he was talking, the way he was presenting himself. It was very impressive and so far he's done a really good job.”

Arsenal predicted XI vs Sunderland: Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaeres, Odegaard; Saka, Tzolis, Havertz.

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim reignites feud with Man Utd legends after failed tenure - 'they talk a lot'
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim reignites feud with Man Utd legends after failed tenure - 'they talk a lot'

Ruben Amorim had to deal with constant opinions during his Manchester United tenure as former players cast their views and the now AC Milan boss has fired a dig at them

View 2 Images Ruben Amorim has taken a swipe at Man Utd's former players

Former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim has taken charge at the club's former players who now work in the media, claiming they "talk a lot about things" from a different era.

‌



The Portuguese coach is now in charge of AC Milan, landing the job at San Siro just months after he was dismissed by the Old Trafford hierarchy. Amorim presided over United's worst-ever Premier League finish and won just 24 of his 63 games.

‌



Milan, like United, has a huge history and has ruled Europe in the past with a number of its former greats giving their opinions on the current state of affairs. That was something Amorim regularly had to deal with when he was at the helm in Manchester.

‌



Gary Neville is one of the country's most high profile pundits whilst the likes of Roy Keane, Nicky Butt and Paul Scholes all hold positions within the media and give their take on current affairs, which saw Amorim under the spotlight.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



When pressed on how it feels to have club legends commenting Amorim replied: "I was in a club [Manchester United] in the past with a lot of legends, and they have big opinions, and they talk a lot about things. They lived in a time that was completely different."

The bulk of the United-associated pundits played during their trophy-laden era when Sir Alex Ferguson was in charge. The Red Devils were the dominant force in the Premier League and serially qualified for the Champions League.

Nowadays United are a shadow of the side they once were. Their wait for a league title has extended to 13 years and they're by no means regulars at Europe's top table.

‌



View 2 Images Ruben Amorim struggled throughout his Man Utd tenure (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Scholes once claimed that Amorim was not "the right man" and doesn't "get the club" before his United exit - with the Milan coach saying at the time that the former players "didn't have all the information" when they made their comments.

"I think it's normal," he said. "I think it's a fact that me, as a manager of Manchester United, I think we are underachieving. We should have more points, especially this season. So I take that naturally.

Article continues below

"Sometimes they don't have all the information and they see Manchester United with the standards that they lived here, always winning. So it's hard for them to see their club in this situation."

Sports.title: Nathaniel Mendez-Laing, 34, charged with assaulting wife as ex-Premier League star set for trial
Sports.content:
Nathaniel Mendez-Laing, 34, charged with assaulting wife as ex-Premier League star set for trial

Nathaniel Mendez-Laing, who played for Cardiff City in the Premier League, attended Magistrates Court where he learned his trial date

View 3 Images Nathaniel Mendez-Laing now plays for MK Dons (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

MK Dons player Nathaniel Mendez-Laing has appeared in court, where he has denied claims he assaulted his wife.

The former Premier League ace stands accused of attacking his wife, Saira Mendez-Laing, while they were in their home in Shenstone, Staffordshire. The incident was alleged to have taken place in June.

He was arrested and charged with assault by beating after the police were called to their house. In magistrates' court on Friday September 11, he denied one count of assault by beating.

Mendez-Laing was on crutches as he arrived wearing a black suit with white shirt. During his appearance at Cannock magistrates' court, he only confirmed his name, age and address.

In August, it's understood the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) authorised charges.

View 3 Images Nathaniel Mendez-Laing appeared in magistrates' court (Image: Instagram)

The MK Dons ace was freed on conditional bail by the court. This was granted by District Judge Joseph O'Connor, who also stated the player will stand trial next January.

Mendez-Laing made 20 Premier League appearances for Cardiff City, where he contributed four goals and one assist.

He now plays for the Dons in League One, having moved to the club from Derby County last summer. While he was born in Birmingham, he is a Guatemala international.

He qualifies for the Central American country, who he has amassed 20 caps with, as both his mother and grand mother hail from the Latin American nation.

View 3 Images Mendez-Laing played in the Premier League with Cardiff City (Image: 2018 AMA Sports Photo Agency)

The player chose to represent Guatemala having previously made appeared for the England U17s when he was a youngster.

Throughout his career, the wide midfielder has also represented Wolverhampton Wanderers, Peterborough, Sheffield United, Portsmouth, Shrewsbury, Cambridge United, Rochdale, Middlesbrough and Sheffield Wednesday.

Mendez-Lain and Saira married in June last year. After they tied the knot, the Dons uploaded a congratulatory post on the club's social media accounts.

His club have said they will not comment on ongoing legal proceedings.

Sports.title: Man Utd disadvantage brushed off by Enzo Maresca ahead of derby - 'It happens in football'
Sports.content:
Man Utd disadvantage brushed off by Enzo Maresca ahead of derby - 'It happens in football'

Manchester United will host neighbours Manchester City having played in midweek, but the Red Devils' game was two days later than their rivals

View 2 Images Man City have enjoyed two days more rest time ahead of the Manchester derby

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca insists Manchester United "are going to be ready" despite them having 48 hours less preparation time for Sunday's derby.

‌



The two rivals come together at Old Trafford this weekend in what is a first major test for both sides - and both teams come into the match off the back of wins to kick off their Champions League campaign.

‌



City won 2-0 at Porto on Tuesday evening before United hammered Sabah 4-0 on Thursday - meaning Michael Carrick's side have less recovery and preparation time than their opponents.

‌



But Maresca has referenced a similar scenario last season, which saw City as the ones with the reduced preparation time. It came before they faced Arsenal this time last year, but the Gunners had faced Athletic Bilbao on the Tuesday whilst City took on Napoli on the Thursday.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Maresca told BBC Sport: "To be honest, the club mentioned to me that it happened exactly the same last year when the club played Napoli and then, after two days, played Arsenal. Sometimes it happens in football. I don't have any doubt that Man United are going to be ready for that. It just matters to adapt."

When pushed on how Michael Carrick would look to use his resources with a turnaround of less than 73 hours, the City boss simply said: "That's a question for Michael. The only thing I can say is it happened and you need to adapt."

Last season former City boss Pep Guardiola joked he was taking his players "hiking in the mountains" so that they could suitably prepare for the game at Emirates Stadium, which they later drew 1-1 after Gabriel Martinelli scored an equaliser in injury time.

‌



View 2 Images Man Utd made light work of Sabah on Thursday night (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

City head to Old Trafford, where they were beaten 2-0 last season in the first game of the Carrick era, with a 100 percent record after three games.

United meanwhile were denied the win at Everton by a stoppage time strike from Ainsley Maitland-Niles. It was the third game in succession that the Red Devils had conceded twice as questions remain over the team's defence.

Article continues below

"We know we have to put in a really good performance and do a lot of good things to get the result we want," said Carrick.

Sports.title: Liverpool vs Fulham - eight players to miss Anfield clash including £85m ace
Sports.content:
Liverpool vs Fulham - eight players to miss Anfield clash including £85m ace

It will be a Liverpool reunion for Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa, but things are not going to be easy for him, and Reds boss Andoni Iraola

View 2 Images Cody Gakpo is one player who will be absent for Liverpool (Image: Justin Setterfield, Getty Images)

Eight players will be missing when Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa reunites with his former side Liverpool at Anfield. The former Reds defender takes his team to Merseyside in desperate need of a positive result.

‌



Fulham have been defeated in all three of their Premier League matches, losing to Chelsea, Sunderland and Crystal Palace. Meanwhile, Liverpool are gathering momentum under Iraola.

‌



They easily beat Ipswich Town 2-0 in their last Premier League match, before overcoming Atletico Madrid 2-1 in the Champions League. It's a big contest for both sides, who share a lengthy list of absentees. Mirror Football take a look at who will be missing for both sides.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool

The primary concern for Liverpool centres on the fitness of Cody Gakpo. The forward sat out the victory over Atletico and faces a late fitness assessment ahead of the Fulham fixture.

"Cody we will see. He didn't train yesterday," Iraola said. "Today we will try with him and let's see if he's ready for tomorrow or we need to wait for the next one."

‌



Should he fail to prove his fitness, he will join defender Joe Gomez on the treatment table. The England man sustained an injury during pre-season and has yet to return to the first-team squad.

While he is edging closer to a comeback, this weekend's fixture may arrive too soon for him. Federico Chiesa is also anticipated to be unavailable having picked up a muscle injury in the latter stages of pre-season. There is currently no indication of when he will make his return.

‌



Three further longer-term injury concerns remain sidelined, with Giovani Leoni, Conor Bradley and Hugo Ekitike all continuing their respective rehabilitation programmes.

In an encouraging boost for Iraola, he has confirmed that summer signing Bradley Barcola is expected to be fit after being substituted with cramp during the victory over Atletico. "We still need to train this afternoon. Barcola was just cramps. We have to evaluate how he is today, but there's no injury. He should, I think, be available, if everything goes normal."

Fulham

Fulham have relatively little to concern themselves with on the injury front, with just two players expected to sit out the match. Club captain Tom Cairney will be absent as he continues his recovery from a minor knee procedure last month.

‌



Young striker Jonah Kusi-Asare is yet to feature in any matchday squad this season. He has made 10 first-team appearances for the club, and was hampered by a knee injury last season.

View 2 Images Arbeloa has endured a difficult start to life at Fulham (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

The match will pit Arbeloa against Iraola, a man he knows well from their time together in Spain. "I played with Andoni in the national team, and obviously we faced each other many, many times in La Liga.

Article continues below

"I know him very, very well. I saw him when he was the coach of Mirandés, Rayo Vallecano, and after in Bournemouth, so I know that he's an amazing coach, and I'm not surprised that now he's the coach of Liverpool.

"He has been doing amazing work here in the Premier League, and now in Liverpool you can see they are playing in the style that he's always playing with his teams, and of course it will be so difficult for us tomorrow."

Sports.title: Michail Antonio returns to English football nearly two years after brutal car crash
Sports.content:
Michail Antonio returns to English football nearly two years after brutal car crash

Michail Antonio spent a period with Qatari side Al-Sailiya following his exit from West Ham after his devastating car crash but the Jamaican forward has now made a return to English football

View 2 Images Michail Antonio has finally found his next club (Image: Getty Images)

Michail Antonio has penned a one-year deal with Watford to make his return to English football. The former West Ham star has been without a club since leaving Qatari side Al-Sailiya in the summer.

‌



Antonio, now 36, had been in the Middle East for a brief spell having been a free agent following a devastating car crash in December 2024.

‌



Speaking after his move was made official, Antonio said: “It’s a good set of boys here. They are focused and ready to show their abilities this season.

‌



“Watford is a big club and hopefully I can come in and bring success and help wherever I can. I’ve scored a few goals against Watford! So hopefully I can score some for Watford now when I’m fully up to speed."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Antonio could make his debut for his new club this weekend as Watford come up against Stoke City at Vicarage Road. The Hornets currently sit 12th in the Championship after six games.

Antonio’s move signals his first return to English football following his exit from West Ham. Prior to that, he was involved in a car crash in December 2024, and was close to losing his life.

Speaking to the BBC about the crash, Antonio said: "It's weird, because the whole way through this, I have been told that I was awake and was speaking to everybody - the police, the people, and the person who found me.

‌



"My leg was completely shattered and they got me out and put a splint on it by the side of the car. Everyone believed I got an air ambulance out, but the helicopter couldn't get off the ground because of the storm, so I was driven to the hospital."

View 2 Images Michail Antonio has not made an appearance in English football since leaving West Ham (Image: Getty Images)

On seeing the wreckage of his car, he added: "It gave me a weird feeling in my stomach. It just made me realise how close I was to dying. I had seen the pictures but it was 10 times worse in person. The car was an absolute mess. It was difficult for me."

Article continues below

Antonio has represented Reading, Cheltenham Town, Southampton, Colchester United, Sheffield Wednesday and Nottingham Forest throughout his career. He joined West Ham in 2015 and went on to score 83 goals in 323 appearances for the Hammers, while he helped the side to the Conference League title in 2023.

Antonio was previously close to moves to both Leicester City and Brentford over the past year but neither side agreed a deal with the Jamaican international.

Sports.title: Chelsea transfer target Lamine Camara speaks out on failed deadline day move
Sports.content:
Chelsea transfer target Lamine Camara speaks out on failed deadline day move

Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara was on the verge of a deadline day switch to Chelsea this summer only to see the rug pulled from beneath his feet and the move cancelled

View 2 Images Lamine Camara saw a deadline day switch to Chelsea collapse (Image: Getty Images)

Lamine Camara insists he is trying to put his failed move to Chelsea behind him. The Monaco midfielder looked to be on the verge of a deadline day switch to Stamford Bridge this summer.

‌



The Blues had agreed a deal with the Ligue 1 side on the final day of the window, with a £47m move in place. But the deal fell through at the 11th hour, with Monaco in no mood to sell due to Folarin Balogun’s expected switch to Everton - albeit that move fell apart as well.

‌



Camara has now spoken out on the failed Premier League switch for the first time and is keen to move on. He said: “It was a somewhat turbulent and difficult time.

‌



“But that’s part of a player’s life. I tried to remain professional, avoid dwelling on it, and move on so I could quickly focus on the upcoming match in Paris (September 4, a 2–1 win). Once it was over, there was no point thinking about it.”

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



He added: “Did I want to go to Chelsea? Saying that now would imply I’m no longer fully present with the team. Yes, there was a possibility I might leave, but it didn’t happen at the last minute. These things happen. Look at the example of Julian Alvarez with Atlético Madrid. It happens all over the world, and I’m trying to turn the page as quickly as possible to focus on the season.

“If it doesn’t come back around, it will be because I gave up or didn’t work hard enough. If I keep going like this, I know I can help the team perform well. Football moves fast, and perhaps other chances will arise. But for now, I’m staying focused on the season.”

Camara was intended to be a direct replacement for Enzo Fernandez, with the Argentine completing a big-money switch to Manchester City.

‌



Monaco sporting director Thiago Scuro gave his take on the move in the days after the window closed. He said: "We started to open negotiations with Chelsea for Lamine. I informed the player directly myself. I called him.

View 2 Images Camara was seen as a potential replacement for Enzo Fernandez (Image: Getty Images)

“I informed his agent as we always do. Very open. We had discussions between the conditions for Lamine to go to Chelsea. At the same time, the medical discussion was ongoing with Balo. And what happened was that around 10:00pm in our time here, maybe a bit earlier, Everton realised that okay, there's no problem. We are ready to do let's sign the contract.

‌



"Chelsea was always testing and trying. 'What about Lamine? What about Lamine?' I've been talking to them from the last 10 days. As soon as we got the information, yes, we did came back to Chelsea and told 'okay, we have our deal there'.

"There is no deal on Lamine because it's also fair to do this. It's also part of the game. There's no reason that this kind of discussions or dynamic on the last day of the transfer window which all of us decided to be on the last day trying to find solutions with the clock ticking in our neck that now this kind of interaction becomes the bad guys in the room that Monaco is not fair, Monaco is not right. Everybody is very fair and nice in football industry just Monaco is not too much. So this is the storytelling.

"We informed again everyone that there was no deal with Chelsea. We progressed. Premier League has a mechanism which you can request one extra hour to finish the paperwork. This was done five minutes to close the transfer window there for us to finish all the paperwork between Monaco and Everton and Balo. I signed the contract. Everton signed the contract.

Article continues below

"At the last moment the player decided not to sign and basically the allegation of Balo is that 'I'm not feeling well by the way the club treated me. I'm not feeling well'. By the way, the medical department of Everton brought doubts about my future or my healthy. I have nothing. So, I'm not comfortable to sign a loan contract here. And that's the way we finish our transfer window."

Sports.title: Ballon d’Or shortlist shows up Premier League’s attacking failings – but tide could be turning
Sports.content:
Premier League representation is low when it comes to the 16 attacking players on this year’s Ballon d’Or shortlist. Manchester United’s Bruno Fernandes and Manchester City’s Erling Haaland are there but Cole Palmer, one of the nominees in 2025, is out after an injury-hit year and English football’s shift towards physicality and set pieces last season is summed up by none of the forwards from the best team in the country making the cut.

The trio giving Arsenal a presence – Gabriel Maghalhães, Declan Rice and William Saliba – are all defensive minded. Arsenal won the league but their forwards are not regarded as elite. Injuries played a part, denying Martin Ødegaard, Kai Havertz and Bukayo Saka fluency, but Mikel Arteta’s side were not loved by neutrals. There was respect rather than admiration for their defensive rigour. There was an argument that a lack of ambition after going 1-0 up stopped Arsenal from beating Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League final.

It was a close-run thing, but a second consecutive European title for PSG was a victory for attacking football over the Premier League’s attrition. Luis Enrique’s side keep beating English opponents, and there was a similar vibe at the World Cup. Games flowed more in North America, in part because of officials clamping down on the “meat wall” at set pieces.

As for England, Thomas Tuchel’s plan to tap into the Premier League’s physicality failed. England retreated in their semi-final defeat by Argentina. It is also significant that not until Anthony Gordon’s goal against Argentina did an England attacker who played in the Premier League last season score at the World Cup.

“Spanish football demands a different level of tactical and technical intelligence,” Gordon has said since leaving Newcastle for Barcelona. “In England, sometimes intensity can cover up mistakes. You can miscontrol the ball and still recover by winning the next physical battle.”

The English top flight’s appeal partly rests on those bruising qualities but the grind went too far last season. How many classic games can you remember? Some of the top sides having disappointing campaigns did not help but across the board there was grumbling about an over-reliance on set pieces and goalkeepers being squashed during elaborate corner routines. Anthony Barry, Tuchel’s assistant, noted that the game had become congealed in the middle. There was an emphasis on long throws and timewasting. The league was harder to watch.

View image in fullscreen Anthony Gordon has said Spanish football demands a ‘different level of tactical and technical intelligence’. Photograph: Newhouse Media/MB Media/Getty Images

Now comes the shift. One of the themes during the first three weeks of the campaign has been the pace quickening. Lawmakers have reacted. The five-second countdown and threat of a restart reversal at goalkicks and throw-ins have forced teams to think twice about timewasting. The 10-second time limit on players leaving the pitch at substitutions has helped and a trial with tactical timeouts mean an outfield player will have to go off for at least a minute after the restart of play if their side’s goalkeeper has gone down injured.

Early days, of course, but the football has been enjoyable and the numbers are encouraging. There have been four matches in which both teams have had 14 shots this season, compared with only one at the same stage last year. According to Opta, the average ball-in-play time has increased from 55min 23sec during the 2025-26 campaign to 57min 14sec. Delay times are down from 29.2sec to 26.7sec. Excluding penalties, the percentage of goals from set pieces has dipped from 27.5% to 23.5%.

There are more fast breaks per game (2.27 compared with 1.94), more shots per game via fast breaks (1.9 compared with 1.75) and more goals from fast breaks per game (0.43 from 0.23). Chelsea, more transitional under Xabi Alonso, are flowing and have been involved in some wild games. Liverpool have replaced Arne Slot with the counterpressing Andoni Iraola. Newcastle have been rapid under Matthias Jaissle, who has played to the strengths of Harvey Barnes and Anthony Elanga. Roberto De Zerbi seems an outlier at Tottenham, who need to speed up. Manchester City may soon want more incision from Enzo Maresca. The Italian favours a methodical style but even Pep Guardiola was moving away from obsessive control last season. There is a sense that some managers are closer in style to Jürgen Klopp than Guardiola at the moment. Alonso’s style has seemed very similar to Klopp so far. His willingness to let talent breathe is also quite like Carlo Ancelotti; Palmer has spoken about being allowed more freedom to roam under Alonso.

Perhaps there will be a correction as teams wise up to each other, Europe kicks in and injuries bite. Perhaps it will amuse you to hear that Arsenal remain top for delaying at a corner (with an average of 43.2sec). Then again, last Sunday delivered the season’s first clash between potential title rivals – Arsenal taking on Chelsea at the Emirates Stadium – and the action was breathless. Chelsea did not hold back and it was interesting that Arsenal welcomed the end-to-end openness.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Havertz was full of imagination up front and Ødegaard, Arsenal’s creative hub, dominated. It is a fascinating development. Defence was Arsenal’s greatest asset last season; Rice was more influential than Ødegaard in midfield. Now the Norwegian looks rejuvenated. Fitness helps but so does greater freedom. Chelsea did not shut the game down, so Ødegaard ran it. The best player in the best team was not a defender. At those levels Ødegaard looks as good as Fernandes.

View image in fullscreen Florian Wirtz has struggled to adapt to the pace of the Premier League. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Richard Sellers/Apl/Sportsphoto

This matters. Florian Wirtz, a star in Alonso’s champion Bayer Leverkusen side, has come to England and found the pace difficult at Liverpool. The Premier League needs top talent to feel it can shine. The three Bayern Munich forwards on the Ballon d’Or shortlist – Harry Kane, Luis Díaz and Michael Olise – moved from English teams. PSG’s Ousmane Dembélé and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia are fresh for the business end of the Champions League in part because they aren’t being pushed to the limit by teams such as Brentford and Bournemouth on the weekend. Jude Bellingham, England’s jewel, has never played in the Premier League. Vinícius Júnior toyed with moving to Arsenal but stayed with Kylian Mbappé at Real Madrid.

The Premier League is the strongest and most competitive in Europe. Yet there has been a talent drain. It is easy to imagine the best forwards feel they will have more fun creating and scoring against less intense Bundesliga defences and have the freshness to compete for the Champions League, international tournaments and for individual prizes.

Look at how the four semi-finalists at the World Cup were well represented by Premier League defenders and defensive midfielders but not by wingers and strikers. Where are the stars? Those who have left have mostly not been replaced, which is why the Premier League could do with Bradley Barcola shining at Liverpool after his arrival from PSG.

Barcola succeeding could convince others to follow. If the France winger is worn down, though, it could have the opposite effect. The Premier League has to be careful. The new measures to tackle timewasting could be a gamechanger. There were only four added minutes at the end of each half when Arsenal beat Chelsea. It felt refreshing.

Sports.title: Kobbie Mainoo moves from outsider to main man after summer of hurt
Sports.content:
It was a sight the England press pack became increasingly used to seeing after the team’s World Cup matches over the summer. Kobbie Mainoo was invariably the first to leave the dressing room, walk through the mixed zone – eyes dead ahead, features impassive – and board the bus.

It was as if he could not get out of the stadiums quick enough and the further England progressed the more pronounced it started to feel. There was a real gap between Mainoo and the next England player to depart the stadium in the knockout rounds. The Manchester United midfielder is inscrutable, even in the heat of battle. It is part of his enviably unflappable temperament. It was no great leap to imagine what lay behind the mask – tremendous frustration as Thomas Tuchel kept on leaving him out.

Mainoo did not play a single minute at the tournament. He was an unused substitute all the way to the semi-final exit against Argentina, and when everyone expected to see him in the third-place playoff against France he did not make the bench. The Football Association said before the game he had picked up an unspecified injury.

For Mainoo it was a lost summer and yet it was physically and mentally draining all the same, what with the training and travel; the demand to stay focused as he waited and waited. Like every player who was part of a squad that reached the final weekend of the World Cup, he reported late for pre-season training with his club. Mainoo played the last half hour of United’s final friendly against Milan and that was it. On the opening weekend of the season, he was fit enough only to be a substitute at Hull, coming on with 23 minutes to go and United 2-0 down, en route to a damaging defeat.

There has been a spotlight on Mainoo, with some fans wondering how he would react to the suffocation of his World Cup dream; his treatment by Tuchel, who preferred Elliot Anderson and Declan Rice in the deeper midfield positions and, also, at various times, Reece James, Jude Bellingham, Jordan Henderson, Morgan Rogers and Nico O’Reilly. Nobody should have worried. Mainoo is made of stern stuff. United regeared their midfield to the tune of £155m during the transfer window, adding Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba. Baleba has not yet played because of injury, but as United prepare for Sunday’s derby at Old Trafford, it is Mainoo who has reasserted himself.

The 21-year-old has been outstanding in each of United’s matches since the opener at Hull – against Ipswich, Everton and then Sabah in the Champions League on Thursday night. The question for Michael Carrick in the derby will be Mainoo and who in front of the back four.

View image in fullscreen Kobbie Mainoo in action against Sabah in United’s 4-0 Champions League win. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Richard Sellers/Apl/Sportsphoto

There is a reason why the United support have adapted the lyrics to Billy Ocean’s Love Really Hurts Without You to declare that their team cannot play without Mainoo. A couple of statistics. In the past three games, he has attempted 211 passes and completed 201, which represents extraordinary security on the ball – particularly given the frequency with which he has it. Also, the degree of risk inherent to so much of what he does.

Then there is the number that shows he made a game‑high 15 defensive contributions against Ipswich and Everton. He is improving out of possession. As much as anything, though, it is the quickness of the feet, the hip-shaking feints and changes of direction; how he simultaneously keeps his opponents on their heels and recalibrates United’s angles of attack.

Mainoo, of course, has already made his big comeback this year. Ruben Amorim could not fit him into his 3-4-2-1 system; the Portuguese did not trust him defensively. But even so, it continues to feel absurd that Amorim did not give him a single start in the Premier League last season. Mainoo’s first in the competition came in January against City at Old Trafford after Carrick had taken over.

It was the first match of Carrick’s second spell as the club’s manager and nobody really knew how it would go. “The players … maybe myself [as well], the coaches, obviously you guys in the media,” Carrick says. Everything came together in spectacular fashion, United winning 2-0, Mainoo straight back into the groove that had helped him win over Amorim’s predecessor, Erik ten Hag.

If it was an ignition point for Carrick, it was the same for Mainoo, whose form for the remainder of the season helped to drive United to a third-place finish and convince Tuchel to take him to the World Cup. As an aside, Mainoo v Anderson, who completed a £116m move from Nottingham Forest to City in July, will be box office. Anderson was a target for United before City blew them away with their offer. He called City “the kings of Manchester” on the day he signed.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

United’s dominance of the derby in January was almost total and a key takeaway was the slick first-time football they played. Remember the passing sequence when Rayan Cherki was triangulated by Matheus Cunha, Luke Shaw and Bruno Fernandes? The click was immediate for Carrick. This is the type of stuff that he wants; what he needs to see more of against City as he hopes to locate a bit of early-season momentum.

View image in fullscreen Kobbie Mainoo had a delayed start to the league season because of his involvement with England at the World Cup. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

Carrick knows a deep-sitting tempo-setter when he sees one, the player of the pass before the pass, and he doubled down on this sort of technician with his summer reboot, especially in Tielemans. It was also noticeable that when the luckless Mason Mount, who is back from his latest injury, came on for Tielemans against Sabah, he did so in a deeper midfield role. Carrick’s idea is to play through the middle. It is about balls to feet, timing, distances.

“It was nice to get Mason on in the second half and Andrey Santos [for Mainoo] and keep seeing the same things,” Carrick says. “It’s the combinations and connections. Taking the ball and playing close together at times. We have the technical ability for the boys to take the ball in the middle of the pitch. A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding … where each of them want the ball, which we are developing. It’s probably something that we’ve done a bit more of this season.”

Carrick is expected to start Tielemans alongside Mainoo with Fernandes as the third midfielder. They will be up against Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Cherki. It is a mouthwatering showdown. It will be where the derby is won or lost.

Sports.title: West Ham cut loose to hit Wrexham for six and go top of Championship
Sports.content:
West Ham secured their fourth league win in a row as they returned to the top of the Championship with a thumping 6-0 win over Wrexham at the London Stadium. It was a marvellous display of attacking football from Nuno Espírito Santo’s side, who swept to victory with room to spare and six different scorers.

Jarrod Bowen got the ball rolling after 28 minutes, Joël Piroe made it two before the break, then Konstantinos Mavropanos, Taty Castellanos, Mohamadou Kanté and Manor Solomon all scored in the second half as the Welsh side were dealt a hiding. The performance was further evidence the Hammers are finding their feet in the second tier after failing to win any of their first three games following Premier League relegation.

They should have led inside seven minutes, Castellanos sending a free header from Solomon’s cross over from six yards. Bowen then got clear in the box from a quick throw, but his shot was turned against the crossbar by a reflex save from Anthony Patterson. From the corner that resulted, Mavropanos headed a foot wide at the far post.

Piroe was guilty of an awful miss midway through the half, leaning back and blasting high into the Wrexham fans behind Patterson’s goal. Bowen showed him how it was done a minute later. Morato’s cross from the right was timed perfectly into the six-yard box, where the home side’s captain was arriving ahead of Jacques Ekomié to guide it into the far corner.

Mavropanos cleared off the line from George Dobson with Mads Hermansen beaten, which proved to be the closest Wrexham would come to a goal. Castellanos stayed onside and strode on to a through pass before unselfishly squaring the ball for Piroe to make it 2-0 before the break.

Patterson prevented Solomon from putting the game beyond Wrexham in the first two minutes of the second half, racing from his goal to smother the forward’s low shot. It would be a momentary reprieve and under a minute later it was 3-0. From Bowen’s corner, Mavropanos was left free inside the six-yard box to head home.

Bowen flashed a shot inches wide after cutting inside as the besieged visitors teetered on the edge of an all-out collapse in east London. West Ham’s fourth came from a Wrexham corner. A poor ball into the box was collected by Kyle Walker-Peters, who dashed away on the counter, exchanging passes before teeing up Castellanos to slot the ball into the corner.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Kanté came off the bench and made it 5-0, a lovely rising finish after being sent clear by Solomon, then the Israel international completed the rout with a deflected shot via a post.

Sports.title: Premier League news: Iraola values Wirtz’s work ethic; Moyes backs ‘senior citizen’ Grealish
Sports.content:
1. Wirtz’s worth ‘not all about statistics’ Andoni Iraola has insisted Florian Wirtz should be judged by his influence on Liverpool rather than statistics and believes the player’s impact will increase as his rapport with a new-look attack develops. Wirtz impressed in Liverpool’s defeat of Atlético Madrid on Wednesday, having also produced some of his best performances last season in the Champions League. But he has also come in for criticism this season for the amount of times he has conceded possession. The £116m Germany international has one assist and no goals in the Premier League so far. “Flo played very well against Atlético Madrid and I also think he has been unlucky,” said Iraola. “I remember the ‘goal’ he scored against Nottingham Forest; they gave it live and then VAR disallowed it. He could have had very good assists but we haven’t finished them. That is why you cannot just play because of the numbers. “Whether a striker scores a lot of goals or he doesn’t, you have to look at the performances. Does he help us to play well? Yes. Well, someone will score the goals and someone will give the assists. I am not too focused on numbers. Nowadays everything is about numbers, everyone tells players you have to assist, you have to score goals. For me, you have to help us play well. Someone will score the goals and I don’t care if it is the midfielders like it was the other day. Someone will score the goals if we are doing well collectively.” Wirtz created an excellent chance for Bradley Barcola against Atlético and Iraola believes the 23-year-old will exert a greater influence as his understanding with the France international and fellow new signing Victor Muñoz improves. “There is an argument to make that the wingers have changed more than anywhere else,” Iraola said. “Now we have new weapons we can use with Bradley and Victor. With Florian, he is key for us. I am not worried because he will quickly learn where Victor prefers the ball or where Bradley prefers the ball. And, also, Bradley in just his second game you could see they already had a good association. I am not very worried.” Andy Hunter

2. Grealish ‘can be a wingers’ role model’ David Moyes has told Jack Grealish he wants him to become a role model at Everton for fellow wingers Tyrique George and Tyler Dibling. Grealish made an immediate impact from the bench against Manchester United last Sunday in his first outing since rejoining Everton on loan from Manchester City. Despite a lack of minutes in pre-season, as he recovered from the fractured foot that curtailed his first campaign with Everton, the 31-year-old could start for Moyes’s side at Tottenham on Saturday. The Everton manager wants Grealish to take on more responsibility this season. “Jack knows when he comes here there is an opportunity for him to play and to show what he can do,” Moyes said. “But I also want him to be a senior professional and a role model. We’ve got Tyrique and Tyler and if ever you are looking at somebody for how to play as a wide player, Jack Grealish would certainly be one of them. “I think both of them could learn an awful lot from Jack and I want him to become that senior citizen among them, somebody who teaches them. We’ve got a mature Jack Grealish now as well in terms of understanding the game and being a team player – not that he is an individual but he plays with an individual style.” Moyes believes there is greater expectation on Grealish given it is his second season at the club and there is a need to fill the creative gap created by Iliman Ndiaye’s departure. “If there is one person who would be able to carry that it would be Jack, just because of the way he is,” he added. View image in fullscreen Jack Grealish made an immediate impact from the bench against Manchester United last Sunday in his first outing since rejoining Everton on loan. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA “He will find it easy to carry expectation and he’ll be happy to do so. That’s his character. Everybody wants Jack to get back to where he was. His first three months for us last season was hugely important in getting us wins so now it is about getting him right to perform at that level again. “He’s had six and a half months out. He’s had no pre-season games, he came on for 15 minutes in the Community Shield, so he’s had no real football and Jack is someone who thrives on the football. He gets himself fit through the games more so than the training. We need to be careful and see how he goes but he’s looking good.” Andy Hunter

3. João Pedro ‘as good as Haaland’, says Alonso Xabi Alonso has claimed João Pedro is at Erling Haaland’s level and similar in style to Karim Benzema. The Chelsea striker has reacted to missing out on Brazil’s World Cup squad by making an excellent start to the season and was named the Premier League’s player of the month on Friday. João Pedro has scored twice in his first three league appearances and has formed an exciting attacking trio with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers. Chelsea have scored 16 goals in all competitions and Alonso did not hold back when asked if the 24-year-old is as good as Haaland. “I would say yes,” Chelsea’s manager said. “If you count how many top strikers we have in the Premier League, I’m sure that João is there. Haaland for sure is there. So I would rate him that way.” The range of João Pedro’s game has added to his threat. Alonso played with Benzema at Real Madrid and sees similarities between the pair. “In many things he reminds me of Benzema,” he said. “He is good in the box, he is good out of the box, he is good coming to his left side, he is good with the head, he is very complete, he is intelligent. Still young, still things to develop, but many, many absolutely outstanding qualities.” Chelsea host Hull on Saturday afternoon and will be looking for a strong home performances after fighting back from 2-0 down to beat Leeds 6-3 in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday. View image in fullscreen João Pedro has scored twice in his first three league appearances for Chelsea. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters Palmer was key to the comeback and revealed that Alonso, who had rotated heavily, ripped into his players at half-time against Leeds. “I was angry with myself that I didn’t help the players to play better or have a better feeling,” Alonso said. “There is a moment that you try to explain what is not working well, try to make preparations and then there is a moment that you need to kick their arse a little bit, in a nice way. It worked – not for me but the players who came on with a better quality and better everything in the second half.” Chelsea will again be without Moisés Caicedo. The midfielder is yet to start this season and Alonso does not want to risk him. Jacob Steinberg

4. De Zerbi wants exile Richarlison to stay Roberto De Zerbi insists he does not regret the handling of Richarlison’s situation at Tottenham after the forward was omitted from his Premier League squad, even though Spurs are yet to score in the competition. De Zerbi said Richarlison had in effect exiled himself by refusing to sign a new contract and repeatedly saying he wanted to leave. The 29-year-old’s absence looks increasingly unfortunate for Spurs after three league matches. They have never gone four league games without scoring at the start of a season. De Zerbi described Richarlison’s omission as a “consequence” of the Brazilian’s actions over the past month and a half. A deadline-day move to Everton, who visit the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday, collapsed after Spurs had signed replacements. Richarlison continues to train with the first team. “If I had decided myself to leave him outside of the squad, I would have regrets,” De Zerbi said. “But the decision has not even been taken by the club.” The Italian said it would be “much better” if Richarlison were in his squad, happy to stay and “maybe to extend his contract, because he is still an important player, he was important last season, we can’t forget. But we can’t forget also the last 45 days.” De Zerbi is missing last season’s three top scorers: Richarlison, João Palhinha, who left for Benfica, and Cristian Romero, who joined Atlético Madrid. Mykhailo Mudryk signed on loan from Chelsea, picked up an injury in training. An ankle scan revealed ligament damage that will keep the winger out for about six weeks. De Zerbi feels the “silly injury”, caused by playing too much after being out for so long, could have been avoided. View image in fullscreen Roberto De Zerbi believes Sávio ‘can score more goals – even if he isn’t Harry Kane.’ Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters Sávio arrived from Manchester City for £75m, closely followed by Omar Marmoush on loan. Marmoush scored only 10 league goals in a season and a half at Manchester City, but was more prolific in the Bundesliga at Eintracht Frankfurt. “In terms of goals he’s not Harry Kane but he can score more goals than he has done in the last two seasons,” De Zerbi said. “If you analyse his qualities, he can score more goals and he has to demand more goals from himself. Even the stupid goals, he has to change his habits after being used to scoring the great goals.” De Zerbi says his players have lacked confidence and freedom on the pitch this season and challenged them to take more risks and show personality “like a big team” and “like big players”. Meanwhile, Lucas Bergvall has signed a new long-term contract. The 20-year-old wanted to leave in the summer but was convinced to stay by De Zerbi. Sam Cunningham

5. Manchester United take action against ticket touts Manchester United believe they have disrupted organised ticketing networks having removed 685 season tickets as part of a contentious ticket touting investigation. The club’s summer crackdown resulted in widespread condemnations from fans and supporter groups after many innocent people faced the threat of sanction. The 1958 this week called for fans to “stand united” against the “season ticket ban fiasco” in a protest before Sunday’s derby against Manchester City as a “line has been crossed”. United released an outcome update on their investigation before this weekend’s action, revealing that 685 accounts have been subject to a ban while 464 supporters received a reduced sanction or final warning. A club statement read: “Bans were issued where there was significant misuse of the ticketing system for financial gain. This included the operation of organised ticketing networks, which were controlling, selling and distributing tickets from hundreds of accounts. “These actions undermine fair access to tickets for genuine supporters and have no place at Manchester United. Our focus now turns to ensuring these tickets are returned to our supporters. All season tickets released through this process will be offered to supporters on the season ticket waiting list.” United say the investigation identified 1,617 accounts that required further review due to what it calls “unusual activity”. Of those stripped of season tickets, 113 failed to respond to requests for further information, 73 did not appeal and 499 received bans upheld by an independent appeals panel. Press Association

6. Jaissle hopes Fernandez-Pardo can face Leeds Matthias Jaissle revealed that summer signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo is edging closer to starting for Newcastle. The 21-year-old forward arrived on Tyneside from Lille on deadline day and has featured as a substitute in Newcastle’s last two matches. Speaking before Monday’s fixture with Leeds, Jaissle said: “Yeah, he’s getting closer. I said that we need to be smart with his load management. Now he’s getting more and more minutes. He has now almost a full training week to Leeds, that helps him a lot. I think it’s the first time now since he arrived, and then we can make the decision on Sunday, maybe even on Monday.” Jaissle was also pleased to see Tino Livramento continue his return from injury as the full-back got 45 minutes of football under his belt with an appearance from the bench during the second half of Tuesday’s Carabao Cup win over Millwall. “I’m happy for him that he got 45 minutes on a high level against a strong opponent in difficult circumstances playing there in Millwall,” the Newcastle manager said. “That makes us proud to see him already on a high level.” Press Association

Sports.title: Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall: ‘I’ve seen all of the meltdowns and it annoyed me’
Sports.content:
Transfer deadline day may be “exciting for everyone”, as Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall puts it, but his experience of that transfer deadline day at Everton hauled him through the same gamut of emotions as every Evertonian. Excitement turned to bewilderment before the conclusion of the window left the midfielder exasperated, but for entirely different reasons to a fanbase left questioning the club’s direction under The Friedkin Group.

How, now, is the mood in the squad? It is the obvious place to start after a deadline day that left David Moyes with fewer players than he had at the beginning, one striker and no cover for either full-back position. It also featured the US international striker Folarin Balogun walking out on a £40m transfer minutes after submitting a deal sheet. “Really good to be honest,” Dewsbury-Hall insists. “Definitely not the same mood as what I’ve seen on the outside. There’s a good mentality this year of: ‘We’ll show everyone.’” Everton’s performances so far this season support that view.

“I’ve seen all of the reactions, all of the meltdowns, and in all honestly it annoyed me a bit,” Dewsbury-Hall says in forthright and insightful fashion. “I get where people are coming from; everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad. But there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded.

“I saw people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’ What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go – and that’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room. Of course we would have wanted to sign a couple more, but we’re happy with what we’ve got and it’s given us more impetus now to move on.”

Moyes has expressed concern over the signals Everton’s transfer business could send to the dressing room at a time when he is trying to push the team on. So has it had a detrimental impact? “Not really, no,” Dewsbury-Hall insists. “I know we’ve got a smaller squad but we’ve got some really good players. Our starting XI is top, a European starting XI.

View image in fullscreen Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall says he needed his move to Everton to avoid his career stagnating. Photograph: Tony McArdle/Everton FC/Getty Images

“I get it, you need a whole squad, but we’ve got 17, 18 players at a really, really good level. I don’t think a couple of years ago it was at that level. Actually I know it wasn’t. Things can be out of your hands in football and that’s what happened for us. But we quickly realised: ‘Hang on a minute, look around the dressing room – top player, top player, top player.’ If we’re doing the right things we can still be successful.”

Dewsbury-Hall will be crucial to those prospects. The midfielder has flourished since his £28m arrival from Chelsea last summer, his game-time and growing influence vindicating the decision to leave Stamford Bridge behind. “I’m in the prime years of my career,” he says. “I couldn’t afford to spend more years stagnating.” The 28-year-old’s influence extends behind the scenes. This summer, following Séamus Coleman’s departure, he was nominated for a new leadership group that was established to compensate for the loss of the long-serving Everton captain.

“Because Séamus has left such a big hole we need a group of experienced lads to crack on together and keep the standards high and to drive things,” Dewsbury-Hall explains. “It’s just the more experienced lads – [Jordan] Pickford, Tarky [James Tarkowski, the new club captain], Jimmy [James] Garner, myself. The ones that have been playing in the Premier League for years or feel like they are settled at the club.

View image in fullscreen Kiernan Dewsbury Hall lets fly in Everton’s impressive 2-2 draw with Manchester United. Photograph: Tony McArdle/Everton FC/Getty Images

“It’s nice [to be voted in after just one season] but it’s definitely an impact I wanted to have. I’m really pleased that the lads look at me as someone that can be important for the dressing room.”

That sense of responsibility is evident in Dewsbury-Hall’s mentoring of fellow midfielder Harrison Armstrong, the 19-year-old who almost joined Nottingham Forest before deadline day only for the furious response of Evertonians at Bournemouth to prompt a U-turn from the club’s owners. “They definitely made their feelings known and obviously it worked,” says Dewsbury-Hall. “Big credit to them for that, they were amazing that day. And I know for a fact it made Harrison feel very good and it helped him. He is a very confident lad and well respected in the dressing room for such a young age.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“If there is anything I can help him with then I will. Shooting’s definitely one because his shooting is sometimes not the best, and I’ve told him that many times. But he’s got pretty much everything else. He always likes to say he’s got a better strike than me so I just tell him to look at the [Crystal] Palace goal [that Dewsbury-Hall scored on the opening day] or the Wolves goal last season. We have good banter.”

The Nottingham-born midfielder is clear in his targets for this season: European qualification, which he contends can be achieved despite the smaller squad, a strong cup run, improvement in his all-round game and a first England call-up. His rising performance levels have not gone unnoticed by Thomas Tuchel, who names his squad next Friday.

Dewsbury-Hall says: “I know I’m the closest I have ever been now. You get a message two weeks before the squad is announced. I got one for the long list for the World Cup and I’ve had one for these next games. It’s nice. It means you are doing OK. It’s a long, long message. It tells you that it’s a legal requirement for us [the Football Association] to tell you in advance that you are in contention and to be available for these dates. It’s a good feeling because you think: ‘OK, I am close,’ but you know you have to keep pushing it to the last minute. It’s up to me. It’s got to be me that forces his hand to choose me. It’s not going to be given to me.”

Nor will anything be given to Everton, but Dewsbury-Hall and company will push on regardless.

Sports.title: ‘Delay the meals’: Mikel Arteta reveals latest maverick Arsenal methods
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has revealed that he likes to set players challenges, such as delaying their meals before matches and making the dressing room hotter, to ensure they are fully prepared for any eventuality.
