Arsenal’s flight to Italy on Tuesday for their Champions League opener against Napoli was delayed for more than five hours, with Arteta forced to cancel his pre-match press conference after the squad arrived in Naples just before 10pm local time.

The disruption proved no handicap as they made it 13 successive league-stage victories in Europe, thanks to Martin Ødegaard’s second-half winner.

Arteta has a reputation for his innovative methods having previously employed pickpockets during pre-season training camps and preparing for a trip to Anfield by pumping crowd noises through a speaker.

The Arsenal manager has now explained how his players have been trained to expect things to go wrong. “I love those challenges. I try to create them in pre-season,” he said. “So when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So, get to the stadium very late, change the routine as soon as the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic, and I don’t want the players, the staff as well, panicking.

“So, when that happens, adapt to it. ‘OK, we have another two or three hours on the plane, how can we use them?’ Play together, spend some time together, sleep, use it, but ­certainly don’t complain and then use it as an excuse because that’s not helpful at all.”

Asked what other methods he has employed, Arteta added: “Just delay the meals, delay the transport, take a different route. We have done many things: make the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less [massage] beds. Those kind of things. Because we are going to have to adapt to different contexts and we will try to anticipate it and create the best possible conditions. But when there is that element of stress or ­surprise on matchday, it’s important [to be prepared].”

Arsenal travel to Sunderland on Saturday night looking to extend their 100% start to the new campaign after being held to a 2-2 draw at the Stadium of Light last year. Leandro Trossard scored Arsenal’s second goal before Brian Brobbey’s late equaliser and Arteta contrasted the Belgium forward’s reaction to leaving in the summer with that of Gabriel Jesus, whohas complained that he was kept in the dark over his future before being sold to Barcelona. “No one told me nothing,” said the Brazilian, who was made to train separately from the rest of Arsenal’s squad before moving to Barcelona. Trossard, meanwhile, was at the Emirates for last week’s win over Chelsea having joined Beskitas in July.

“Very surprised, to be fair, especially because with Gabriel I had an individual talk in the dressing room,” said Arteta. “And the words that we used for each other, it was all about gratitude. So, I don’t know. It’s OK. Sometimes I understand when you have to deliver bad news or news that people don’t expect. Those things are reactive. Somebody has to be the bad cop; if I have to be, I have to be.

“What is important is normally what happens three months later, six months later. When Trossard comes in, he’s in the dressing room with all of us, the atmosphere and the relation you have with all the players that they left, at some point their relationship has been really good. I hope that’s the same case.”

Sports.title: Chelsea hand Pedro Neto new deal in wake of his rejecting Manchester City
Sports.content:
Chelsea have rewarded Pedro Neto’s strong start to the season and commitment to the club by handing the winger a new contract. The Portugal international had summer interest from several Premier League clubs including Manchester City, but indicated a desire to stay and play for Xabi Alonso. He has signed a five-year deal with the option of an extra year and is to receive a pay rise.

Alonso has used Neto as an attacking wingback and the 26-year-old has scored twice in five appearances. Neto, who has registered 40 goal involvements since joining from Wolves for £54m in 2024, follows other leading players at Chelsea in signing new deals. João Pedro, Reece James and Moisés Caicedo have received improved terms this year, and Cole Palmer signed a new deal in 2024 and committed his future to the club in an interview with the Guardian last season.

Chelsea’s owners have a strategy of giving lengthy incentivised contracts. However, the club have demonstrated that being on those multi-year deals will not stop players from receiving pay increases as reward for good performances. Further contract renewals are expected to be announced soon.

Neto’s determination to stay contrasted with the stance of Enzo Fernández, who was sold to City for £125m during the closing hours of the transfer window.

He was not handed a new contract after initial discussions were held. The Argentina midfielder raised questions over his future in March, criticising January’s departure of Enzo Maresca as head coach and sparking talk of a move to Real Madrid by expressing a desire to live in the Spanish capital. Chelsea responded by banning Fernández for two games.

Madrid downplayed their interest in Fernández but the 25-year-old continued to push for a new challenge. City, who appointed Maresca as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, emerged as Fernández’s strongest suitors. Chelsea were prepared to hold on to him if their valuation were not met but concluded that selling was the right long-term move. There was disappointment that one of the team’s senior players did not show better leadership when Chelsea were struggling. They missed out on European qualification after finishing 10th.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca and Enzo Fernandez during their time at Chelsea. They have been reunited at Manchester City. Photograph: Mark Pain/Alamy Stock Photo/Alamy Live News.

Chelsea sacked Liam Rosenior in April and announced Alonso’s appointment in mid-May. They were willing to reintegrate Fernández but he is understood to have submitted a written transfer request. It is understood he also informed Chelsea he had been in contact with a former coach, believed to be Maresca, at the end of last season and during the transfer window.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Stamford Bridge hierarchy concluded that Fernández’s relationship with his teammates was broken after his public comments. Fernández’s representatives have been approached for comment.

Sources have dismissed the idea that Chelsea were bullied into selling Fernández. Neto’s renewal is viewed as the latest evidence that key players have bought into the project and will be rewarded.

Sports.title: Olid’s United on back foot due to late business and unforgiving WSL start
Sports.content:
It was tough watching Manchester United’s players labour ineffectively against the hungry and aggressive press of London City Lionesses in the Women’s Super League’s opening match. Simi Awujo’s late consolation goal did little to ease the mounting concern for a side that have several teams nipping at their heels.

Don’t panic; that has to be United’s message. To an extent, it is very early to be writing the team’s obituary. The new head coach, Eva Olid, had only three weeks to try to implement her ideas about the way the team should play before that match in Bromley on Friday 4 September. That is not long enough for her to peel away Marc Skinner’s imprint on the team.

The forward Monica Jusu Bah did not arrive from the Swedish side Häcken until 28 August and Rebeca Bernal signed from Washington Spirit on 2 September. United’s late business, in regards to their managerial change and transfer activity, has put the team and coaching staff on the back foot, playing catch-up with clubs who got most of their business done early in the window, the better to capitalise on the opportunity for a full pre-season presented by the lack of a major international tournament.

The problem is the spotlight is harsh on the red side of Manchester. The minority owner Jim Ratcliffe’s dismissive comments relating to the women’s team and the lack of serious investment in the squad provide reasons to be somewhat forgiving of the head coach and her charges, their struggles an indictment of a club that seemingly do not fully care.

The focus is said to be on a sustainable investment model recruitment-wise and on developing younger players. In isolation they are admirable goals, but in the context of investment gathering pace at other WSL teams and the relative pocket change required at a club of United’s stature to have a transformatory effect on the women’s side, these goals become shackles.

There is some irony in Olid leaving Hearts and coming to United. She arrived in Scotland to take charge of an amateur team that had avoided relegation only owing to the expansion of the top division and within five years had taken them to professionalism and a Scottish Women’s Premier League title. She felt the level of investment then needed to make Hearts competitive in Europe was lacking and it was announced that she would depart at the end of the season. The WSL and its teams are miles ahead, developmentally, of the SWPL and its sides but Olid has landed at a club that have repeatedly failed to invest substantially enough to make them league or European title challengers.

Olid told the Catalan newspaper Ara that she would have stayed at Hearts “if my project continued”. She said: “I wanted to coach in Europe, but it was a preliminary round and perhaps we would be there for a week and get eliminated. I don’t want to go backwards, I preferred to leave after winning everything because otherwise I would feel frustrated.”

View image in fullscreen Manchester United only lost 2-1 at London City Lionesses last Friday but were outclassed throughout the game. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Frustration was the name of the game at United under Skinner. The former head coach was frustrated with what he regarded as a lack of support in transfer windows and fans grew increasingly frustrated with a lack of sustained progress. United would take a step forward, such as winning the FA Cup in 2024 or reaching the Champions League quarter-finals last season, then fail to push on.

Patience is thin and Olid’s task has been made a lot harder by seven departures and only four additions to what many viewed as an already light squad. Olid has said she has had assurances that United will be active in the winter window. “We have some plans in January about signing players that I really need for my style of play and game model,” she said in her first press conference.

However, United have 12 WSL games before January, plus cup games, and with Chelsea visiting on Sunday and a trip to Arsenal next Saturday, they have an extremely unforgiving start.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Olid deserves time and patience. She is well respected and comes with a wealth of experience in her native Spain across boys’ academy football and women’s football and spent time at Houston Dynamo in the US.

Alongside battling critics unimpressed with the state of the team in their opening WSL game or questioning her managerial pedigree, she must contend with wave after wave of appalling sexist comments on social media that greet her every appearance. That surely will take a toll.

If Olid is able to weather the storm of frustration – which will grow if the team falter while players get used to her philosophy – and to force United to loosen the purse strings, they will be huge accomplishments.

Unfortunately, even success on the pitch is unlikely to end the online comments; it will probably just shift their tone. She deserves better in so many ways. The hope will be that she can build a connection with the playing group that enables them to punch above their weight until reinforcements potentially appear in January.

Their first opportunity to fend off the vultures is when they welcome Chelsea to Leigh and, with the Blues unconvincing in the final third against Aston Villa last Saturday, they can have a little hope.

Sports.title: Phil Parkinson’s future questioned as ‘woeful’ Wrexham handed heaviest loss of Hollywood era
Sports.content:
Phil Parkinson has been warned of pressure in the Wrexham hot seat after they were thumped 6-0 by West Ham United.

Jarrod Bowen, Joel Piroe, Konstantinos Mavropanos, Taty Castellanos, Mohamadou Kante and Manor Solomon netted as the Hammers were a class above their visitors.

3 Parkinson watched his Wrexham side ship six goals at West Ham Credit: Getty

West Ham, who are favourites for promotion back to the Premier League, had six different goalscorers in a league match for the first time in their 131-year history.

It broke their previous record of five, and the convincing victory was also their biggest in 28 years.

Head coach Nuno Espirito Santo has sent them to the Championship summit, whilst his counterpart Parkinson looks up in 16th.

The 58-year-old is in his sixth season as Wrexham boss and has played a big role in their meteoric rise from the National League.

However, according to Scott Minto, the alarm bells may be beginning to ring after a shocking performance, which was described as woeful by talkSPORT commentator Joe Shennan.

'It's very, very bad'

"Of course there'll be pressure," Minto said on commentary, with the 6-0 loss being the heaviest under the Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney ownership. "There's very, very ambitious owners.

"But you have to think about what he's done and he’s earned the right to right this wrong… but this is a really poor run.

"And there are question marks against him maybe with signings, certainly with substitutions, or lack of, tonight."

However, Minto stressed that Wrexham must keep Parkinson's success at the club in mind, despite their recent poor run of form.

"But let's not forget where he's brought this club from and where it is right now," he continued.

3 Wrexham have suffered the biggest defeat since their Hollywood takeover in 2021 Credit: Getty

"The Championship is a long, long season. It's one win in the season in the league.

"But he knows that's not good enough… it's poor, it's not good, it's very, very bad."

Parkinson reflects on West Ham defeat

Speaking to talkSPORT after full-time, Parkinson examined what went wrong with Wrexham's performance at West Ham.

"First of all, as a manager, you've got to analyse it yourself," he began. "They're a good side, we know that.

"The first 25 minutes we were okay in the game and then we conceded two goals, which were moments in and around the box we had to do better.

"We gave a team that were already full of confidence another lift…the next goal kills the game and it was a tough, tough night.

3 West Ham have risen to the top of the Championship with their huge win Credit: Getty

"Against quality opposition we didn't do enough when it was needed tonight."

Parkinson also spoke on his substitutions, having brought on two defenders and just one attacker in the 67th minute when 4-0 down.

"Could I have changed more? I will look at myself, the selection and everything about it."

Wrexham have drawn four of their seven league matches this season, including the stalemate at Welsh rivals Swansea City last weekend.

Southampton are their last opponents ahead of the international break, and Minto revealed just how important it is that they win.

"If they lose that and lose it heavily, that's going to be three long weeks before the international break finishes."

Sports.title: Richarlison transfer collapses as wantaway Tottenham star misses out on second move away
Sports.content:
Richarlison transfer collapses as wantaway Tottenham star misses out on second move away

Richarlison will not join Vasco da Gama after failing to agree personal terms, talkSPORT understands.

The striker had been in talks with the Brazilian club as he eyes an exit from Tottenham Hotspur, who agreed a deal in principle.



2 Richarlison will no longer sign for Vasco da Gama amid a breakdown in talks Credit: Getty

It's understood that Richarlison has approached FIFA in an attempt to terminate his contract at Spurs, which expires in June.

That came after he was omitted from their 25-man Premier League squad for this season.

However, his future has become even more uncertain now that a return to Brazil has collapsed.



Another failed move for Richarlison

Richarlison also missed out on a move back to Everton late on in the summer transfer window.

Spurs had agreed a deal with the Toffees, but the player hit out at the ambiguity over his plans for the season.



The 29-year-old is one of three players who asked to leave Spurs before the deadline, as revealed by boss Roberto De Zerbi.

Richarlison played in their Premier League opener at Brentford, which ended in a 3-0 defeat, and this may have been his last match.



He has scored 32 goals in 134 appearances for the club since signing from Everton in 2022.

Although he helped them win the 2024/25 Europa League, he has mostly underwhelmed in north London.

It remains to be seen if a move away will be finalised, or both Spurs and Richarlison will have to wait until the January window.

2 For now, Richarlison remains on the books at Spurs Credit: Getty



Whilst Richarlison made it clear he wants to leave Spurs, the club also appeared to prepare for a split when they signed Omar Marmoush.

They brought the forward in from Manchester City in an initial loan deal that includes a £60million obligation to buy.

Dominic Solanke has also had regular involvement this season, having featured four times and scored one goal.

Marmoush and Solanke both played in the 2-0 defeat to Newcastle United, with Richarlison left out of the squad.



This also happened during the 0-0 draw with Nottingham Forest last weekend.

And the saga is now expected to continue after he opted out of another move away from the club.

Sports.title: Arsenal sign ‘next Khvicha Kvaratskhelia’ – but highly-rated teenager won’t join immediately
Sports.content:
Arsenal have reached a pre-contract agreement with FC Kolkheti 1913 to sign Andria Bartishvili.

The Premier League champions will officially welcome the 17-year-old in July 2027 when he turns 18.

2 Arsenal have signed highly-rated teenager Bartishvili, who will join next summer Credit: Getty

Bartishvili, a versatile forward who can play out wide or through the middle, has earned two caps for the Georgia U21 side.

He was named as the U17 Player of the Year in the Georgian top flight for 2025 during his second season at Kolkheti.

The teenager is currently loaned out to Iberia 1999 and has been touted as a carbon copy of a Georgia superstar - Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Napoli awarded him his first big break in European football in 2022 as he signed from Dinamo Batumi and later won two Serie A titles.

A move to Paris Saint-Germain followed in January 2025, one that has delivered back-to-back Champions League and Ligue 1 honours.

Kvaratskhelia was even named as the Champions League Player of the Season for 2025/26 as he bagged 17 goal contributions in 16 matches.

Bartishvili has 'potential to become great'

Italian agent Cristian Zaccardo helped bring Kvaratskhelia to Napoli, and also noticed the soon-to-be Arsenal starlet Bartishvili.

"Recently, a lot of talented players have appeared in Georgia, one of such players is Andria Bartishvili," he said via the Standard.

"This 16-year-old attacking midfielder has the potential to become a great player.

"I saw Khvicha Kvaratskhelia play two years before he moved to Napoli, he was already a phenomenal player. I met him and then recommended him to Napoli."

2 Bartishvili has been tipped for similar success to his fellow Georgian Kvaratskhelia Credit: Getty

Kvaratskhelia is now in contention to win the Ballon d'Or, the most prestigious individual award in football.

He was named on the 30-man shortlist and has been tipped to be the main rival to Harry Kane for this year's honour.

According to the BBC, Arsenal's move for Bartishvili was led by Maurizio Micheli, the assistant to sporting director Andrea Berta.

Micheli is said to have played a role in discovering Kvaratskhelia when he was chief scout at Napoli.

The deal to sign Bartishvili has been announced just days after it was revealed that Mylo Bernard has joined Arsenal from Crystal Palace.

A first-year scholar at the Gunners, he netted in excess of 40 goals for his former club's youth sides last season.

Sports.title: Man United told to drop Marcus Rashford for Manchester derby in ‘unfair’ decision
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford will be desperate to start against Manchester City, but Michael Carrick should pick Matheus Cunha over him.

That's the view of Darren Bent, despite noting that he has not had a real chance to impress for Manchester United so far this season.



3 Rashford will eye a start against City after being rested during the week Credit: Getty

Rashford will hope to appear in his first Manchester derby since they met in the 2024 Community Shield, having now returned to action for his boyhood club after loan spells at Aston Villa and Barcelona.

The left winger has started in two of the Red Devils' three Premier League games this season, coming off the bench in their first outing.

He did not play in the 4-0 win over Sabah FK in the Champions League on Thursday night, with the clash against City two days away.



Rashford has scored five goals and assisted one other in 22 matches for United against their local rivals, but former Villa striker Bent has explained why he wouldn't start him this weekend.

Rashford to be dropped for derby?

On talkSPORT Drive, he responded to Troy Deeney's claim that fans are too lenient with Rashford because he's from their academy, and players such as Matheus Cunha are not given as much time.



"Academy players at any football club always get more time than anyone else, but that's just normal," Bent said. "They're one of your own, of course they're going to get a bit longer."

He added: "With Rashford, you're going to get some Man United fans who have backed him the whole time, even though he's said, 'No, I don't want to come back, I want to stay at Barcelona'.



"You (host Andy Goldstein) still welcomed him back because he's one of your own, you love him, you've always loved him. I think, for the manager, it's a nice problem to have.

"This is not a problem because you've got (Benjamin) Sesko scoring goals now and me, being a former centre forward, I would like to see Sesko play in his position.

"Rashford, to me, looks sharper this season. Cunha's playing really well. (Bryan) Mbeumo's playing well.

3 Bent believes that Carrick should omit Rashford from the starting XI on Sunday Credit: Getty



"At least you've got all these options now that are playing well so, rather than Michael Carrick going, 'What am I going to do this week, none of them are playing well, what do I do?'

"They're all scoring goals, so it's a nice problem...I would opt to go for Mbeumo, Sesko, Cunha from the left."

When asked why he would drop Rashford, Bent said: "The only reason why I feel this is a little bit unfair, and this could be the same for most, is that Mbeumo's getting a good run of games.

"Rashford's not really had a run yet, and you're only going to get the best of Rashford when he's playing, playing, playing."



Goldstein also wondered if such a decision for the Manchester derby would make a difference for Rashford as he is local to the area.

"Of course, it will mean more to him than most," Bent insisted. "He's scored in loads of them as well. I remember when he first burst on the scene, he scored in his third or fourth game.

3 Cunha, who scored against Sabah, has been tipped to play on the left Credit: Getty

"He knows all about it, he's from Manchester, he understands it. But, Michael Carrick ain't got time to worry about that.



"Cunha's playing well, Sesko's playing well. If you believe that's the best combination to get Man United to win, that's what you have to do."

Sports.title: Teddy Sheringham explains why Harry Kane won’t win Ballon d’Or as ex-champion tipped for title
Sports.content:
Teddy Sheringham explains why Harry Kane won’t win Ballon d’Or as ex-champion tipped for title

Harry Kane won't win the Ballon d'Or because of his shortcomings in the Champions League and World Cup.

That's the opinion of Teddy Sheringham, who named the player that he believes is worthy of claiming the honour for a second time.



3 Kane is a Ballon d'Or favourite, but Sheringham would not vote for him Credit: Getty

Kane has made the 30-man shortlist for the 2026 Ballon d'Or, with its ceremony taking place on October 26 in London.

The award is based on success from the previous season and so the 2025/26 campaign will be taken into account this time round, as well as the World Cup.

Across 51 appearances for Bayern Munich, Kane scored a whopping 61 goals and assisted a further seven.



He then netted six times during the World Cup and won a third-place medal with England as captain.

However, fellow former Tottenham Hotspur striker Sheringham told talkSPORT that Kane doesn't have the credentials to win the Ballon d'Or this year.



"Would he get my vote? Not really," he explained to Sam Matterface, Alex Crook and Scott Minto.

"I think he's had a phenomenal season, but the Ballon d'Or winner is normally one that wins the Champions League or the World Cup, or whatever is there at that moment.



"He didn't quite do that, so he's an also-ran for me. Sorry about that, Harry!"

Who should win the Ballon d'Or?

Sheringham was asked who he would vote for to win the award, and revealed that 2024 champion Rodri deserves to be crowned again.

The midfielder, who signed for Barcelona in the summer, won the FA Cup and Carabao Cup with Manchester City last season, during which he featured 33 times.

3 Sheringham believes Rodri is worthy of winning after his World Cup success Credit: Getty



Rodri then played in all eight matches for Spain at the World Cup as they won their first title since 2010 by beating Argentina in the final.

"He's a leader, his teams normally win week in, week out. Manchester City, Spain," Sheringham said.

"I know he's gone now but whoever he plays for, they win."

Have any of the Ballon d'Or nominees won the Champions League and World Cup?

Out of the 30 nominations, Fabian Ruiz is the only player to have won both the Champions League and World Cup.

The 30-year-old featured in nine of Paris Saint-Germain's European fixtures as they won the final against Arsenal on penalties.



Ruiz was also involved in every match that Spain played at the World Cup, with starts coming in four of those.

3 Dembele is the current holder of football's most prestigious solo prize Credit: Getty

His PSG teammate Ousmane Dembele is the defending champion and also among the nominees.

They are joined by stars such as the record eight-time winner Lionel Messi, Lamine Yamal, Jude Bellingham and Erling Haaland.

Sports.title: Man United ban 685 season ticket holders and more given final warning after investigation
Sports.content:
Man United ban 685 season ticket holders and more given final warning after investigation

Manchester United have banned 685 season ticket holders following a summer investigation into touting.

The Premier League club published their findings on Friday and broke down the extent of ticket misuse among supporters.

3 Hundreds of United fans have been hit with season ticket bans Credit: Getty

Unusual activity was identified in 1,617 accounts, all of which are said to have required further review and been contacted so the holders could provide explanations.

No further action has been taken with 468 cases, although another 226 accounts have been issued with a final warning.

Initial season ticket bans were later reduced to restrictions on ticket forwarding for home fixtures and away match applications for 238 accounts.

However, United then explained that the independent appeals panel upheld season-long season ticket bans for 499 accounts, and those supporters can reapply for tickets afterwards.

A further 73 cases had bans that were not appealed, whilst 113 others were suspended as a result of no responses to repeated information requests.

Season ticket bans have been given to 685 accounts in total, with 464 others being hit with reduced sanctions or final warnings.

"Bans were issued where there was significant misuse of the ticketing system for financial gain," the club said.

"This included the operation of organised ticketing networks, which were controlling, selling and distributing tickets from hundreds of accounts."

The season tickets being released are set to be offered to supporters on the waiting list.

Those who have received bans are beginning to receive their refunds.

3 United have revealed the actions they have taken after an investigation Credit: Getty

United fans set to protest over ticket tout response

On Sunday, United will host archrivals Manchester City at Old Trafford for their first Premier League clash of the season.

However, many home supporters will use the match to protest amid the club's crackdown on touting.

United reportedly threatened to withdraw tickets from accounts of loyal supporters who had shared details and single devices, with an apology later being issued.

Then, ahead of their 4-0 win over Sabah FK in the Champions League, some fans were sent messages warning against their attendance.

One shared a text that read: "You don't have a ticket for the Sabah game on Thursday - do not come to Old Trafford."

It also claimed that a fan's season ticket could be deactivated for a future Premier League match if a ticket was not purchased for the Sabah match.

3 United fans will protest before their weekend clash against City Credit: Getty

As per the BBC, United accepted that the wording could have been improved, and they only sent the message after there were several follow-up attempts via email.

The 1958 fan group said: "Manchester United supporter groups are being called upon to all stand together following reports of bans and season ticket sanctions without clear and compelling evidence always being presented.

"For generations, match-going Reds have given their time, money and loyalty to Manchester United, home and away. That loyalty deserves to be treated with respect.

"This is not about one group or one individual. It is about how Manchester United treats its match-going supporters. It may not affect you today, it may not next time but that day is coming for all of us.

"If there is clear, substantive evidence of serious wrongdoing or organised ticket touting, show it.

"No loyal supporter should be treated as guilty without being given a fair opportunity to understand and challenge the case against them."

Sports.title: Wesley Sneijder puts World Cup prize and Cristiano Ronaldo treasure on sale for thousands
Sports.content:
Wesley Sneijder has put some of his career memorabilia up for auction, including his 2010 World Cup Silver Ball award.

The Dutch football legend retired from football in 2019, having starred for the likes of Real Madrid, Inter Milan and the Netherlands national team.

3 Sneijder finished the 2010 World Cup as joint-top scorer with five goals Credit: Getty

Sneijder enjoyed a trophy-laden career, tasting league glory in Holland, Spain and Italy among his 20 major honours.

He was at the peak of his powers in 2010, as he inspired Inter to treble success - including the Champions League - and scored five goals at the World Cup final to fire the Netherlands to the final.

The playmaker continued to star on the European and international stage thereafter, turning out for Galatasaray and Nice before retiring at Qatari side Al Gharafa, and also played at the 2014 World Cup.

Sneijder auctions career mementos

Sneijder's decorated career saw him collect plenty of individual awards and silverware, as well as some cherished memorabilia.

But now, the former midfield superstar has decided to put many of these items up for auction.

Auction platform MatchWornShirt have announced that the Dutchman has partnered with them to sell mementos from his stellar career as part of their 'Legends Collection'.

This includes the Silver Ball award he received as the second-best player at the 2010 World Cup.

To date, Sneijder remains the only Dutch player to have won this World Cup distinction, as he came second to Diego Forlan.

The prestigious award leads the collection of memorabilia and is among several items from his memorable campaign in South Africa set to go under the hammer.

Also being auctioned is the match ball from the quarter-final against Brazil - where he scored twice to fire the Netherlands into the last four.

3 Sneijder was named UEFA midfielder of the season in 2010 after inspiring Inter Milan to European glory Credit: AFP

Alongside the Golden Ball and match ball, Sneijder is also offering his 2010 World Cup participant's medal and his bronze medal from the 2014 World Cup.

These international award items will form part of one of three separate auctions offering different collections.

Sneijder's international career makes up one collection, with the auction set to take place this Friday.

This will be the second of the three auctions, with the first seeing the ex-midfielder offer up a collection of items from his successful years at Inter Milan.

With the first sale taking place earlier on Friday, Sneijder's 2011 Coppa Italia winner's medal and a signed shirt by the Inter squad had already raised €2,708 (£2,323) before it's conclusion.

Ronaldo memorabilia up for grabs

The third of Sneijder's auctions will feature keepsakes from his four-year spell at Galatasaray between 2013 and 2017.

3 Cristiano Ronaldo tasted Champions League glory with Real Madrid in the same season as his treble against Sneijder's Galatasaray Credit: Getty

And top pick here is a match-worn Cristiano Ronaldo shirt from Real Madrid's clash with the Turkish giants in September 2013.

Sneijder was on the pitch for Galatasaray that evening and swapped shirts with Ronaldo after the final whistle, who had scored a hat-trick to help fire Los Blancos to a 6-1 victory.

On the decision to auction his prized possessions, Sneijder shared his delight at fans being able to collect items connected with his all-time career highs.

He said: "These items are tied to matches and moments that have been very special to me. Like the match against Brazil at the 2010 World Cup.

"I think it's great that I can now share these memories with football fans and collectors who appreciate the story behind them just as much."

Sports.title: Tottenham will live to regret giving Roberto De Zerbi so much power
Sports.content:
Tottenham will live to regret giving Roberto De Zerbi so much power

“The cracks are there and Roberto De Zerbi is not very good at signing players.”

talkSPORT’s chief football correspondent Alex Crook did not hold back with his scathing take on the Italian tactician and the task he faces in turning round Tottenham’s fortunes.

6 Roberto De Zerbi and Spurs have had an underwheming start to the season despite splashing the cash this summer Credit: Getty

6 Spurs have not scored a single goal in their opening three matches Credit: Getty

A lavish shopping spree and a summer of optimism appears to have fallen flat in just four weeks.

Tottenham have taken just one point from their opening three games and crucially, are yet to find the net.

With a whopping £314m spent in bolstering a decaying squad, expectation is understandably high for the underachieving north London club.

Spurs’ home fixture with Everton on Saturday already feels like a crucial one with Spurs in familiar territory in 18th place.

As a result, De Zerbi, who worked late-season wonders to steer the club away from relegation, is now firmly under the microscope.

Crook believes there could be further trouble ahead for Tottenham due to the Italian’s huge influence at the club.

Too much trust?

De Zerbi oversees team affairs as well as having a hand in recruitment; however, Crook’s deep dive into his previous transfer affairs shows a less-than-impressive outcome.

“This is a guy who when Tottenham first approached him to be their saviour last season, he turned the job down. He didn’t want to take over midway through the season,” Crook told talkSPORT’s Fiery Fridays podcast.

“He wanted a clean break and to come in, in the summer.

“They chucked a ridiculous amount of money at him, a ridiculous bonus for keeping them in the Premier League but more importantly in Roberto De Zerbi’s eyes, they gave him overall control of recruitment.

6 De Zerbi guided Spurs away from the drop zone on the final day of last season Credit: Getty

“They don’t really have a director of football worthy of the name so not only is he the head coach, he’s also in control of the transfer policy at Spurs.

“All of these signings have been bought for excessive fees in my opinion at the whim of one man.”

Crook continued: “Now I’m not sure whether Tottenham did their homework on Roberto De Zerbi and his time at Brighton.

“You look at the numbers and he was excellent. He took the Seagulls into Europe for the first time in their history.

“They went deep in cup competitions, the football was pleasing on the eye but how many of those players did De Zerbi actually sign himself, how many of those players did he inherit as a gift from the genius that is Tony Bloom and his data-led approach to scouting.

“Well I know he signed two players because this is one of the reasons they ended up falling out, De Zerbi and Bloom, because he didn’t want to be told anymore which players he was inheriting and he wanted to have a say in recruitment.”

6 De Zerbi was instrumental in bringing Ansu Fati to Brighton but the transfer was a forgettable one Credit: Getty

De Zerbi's transfer flops

Crook then identified two signings that he believes typifies De Zerbi’s poor standard of recruitment.

“One of them was Mo Dahoud who came in from Germany and stunk the place out," he began.

"And the other expensive mistake that Brighton made was a player called Ansu Fati and ironically they are going to meet in the Conference League when they take on Monaco.

“He absolutely flopped at the Amex and he was the most expensive player Brighton ever had.

“He was on ridiculous money for very little output.

“What on earth makes Tottenham think this guy can take the lead when it comes to recruitment.”

6 Sandro Tonali is yet to show his best form for Spurs Credit: Getty

'This could end in disaster'

De Zerbi’s summer signings included three players signed for in excess of £80m.

Spurs are yet to see any sign of the level expected of those three stars and Crook has slammed the fees laid out for their marquee summer acquisitions.

“Why did they put in £100million for Sandro Tonali when there was nobody else at the table? They were basically bidding against themselves,” Crook said.

“Why did they pay £85m for Matheus Fernandes? Relegated twice in successive seasons with two different clubs when nobody else was there.

“Manchester United when the price tag was put on his head said ‘ you know what we’re alright, we’re going to sign Carlos Baleba’.

“Why did they pay so much money for Jan Paul van Hecke who is a good Premier League player but not top class. He had one year left on his contract?

6 Crook was critical of the £85m shelled out on Savinho Credit: Tottenham Hotspur FC

“Savinho, £85m. I don’t know if Man City have put the phone down laughing yet. He got two Premier League goals last season

“I think Tottenham’s recruitment has been poor. De Zerbi is already reverting to type, blaming other people. The medical staff came under the microscope didn’t they after they drew at the weekend.

“I think this could end in disaster because what we know about De Zerbi is when things aren’t going his own way he’s very combustible.

“That’s why he never stays at a club for too long and even though he’s been given the keys to the kingdom at Spurs, the cracks are there and he’s not very good at signing players.”

Sports.title: US Open tickets plummet ahead of men's semi-final... to the price of LESS than a Honey Deuce cocktail!
Sports.content:
Tickets for the highly coveted men's semi-final afternoon session at this year's US Open plummeted on resale sites to as low as $19 ahead of the tournament's number one seed Alexander Zverev's meeting with Karen Khachanov.

In the build-up to the final Grand Slam of the year, most of the headlines surrounding tickets to the event centred on their sky-high resale prices, with grounds passes for the first week of the US Open - with a face value of $65 - being sold on the secondary market for upwards of $300.

While the USTA is powerless to stop tickets being sold for miles more than their initial value, the tournament's organisers do receive a 'legal share revenue' from seats sold on Ticketmaster, their official partner.

Weeks later however, the focus is on dropping prices, with the cost of a seat inside the Arthur Ashe nosediving on the eve of the first men's semi-final.

While many fans have eagerly taken advantage of the deals for a seat in the upper levels of the 23,000-plus stadium, the pricier lower bowl of the US Open's show court was visibly more sparse than organisers may have hoped for.

As per ticket resale site StubHub, via journalist Ben Rothenberg, the lowest prices for tickets for Friday afternoon were $19 and $21, with up to five sets of Grand Slam tennis available for the price of less than one of the US Open's trademark Honey Deuce cocktails ($23).

Tickets to the men's semi-final between Alexander Zverev and world No50 Karen Khachanov on the afternoon of Day 13 at the US Open dropped sharply

Tennis tournaments must contend with the absence in the latter stages of stars like last year's winner Carlos Alcaraz

Tickets costing less than one of the tournament's famous Honey Deuce cocktails were available hours before the first serve in the semi-final

Ticket prices on the secondary markets have dropped since last year across the board, with TicketData reporting that the average price of the cheapest ticket across both day and night sessions on Day 13 of the tournament has shifted from $319 in 2025, to $244 today.

Demand remains much higher for Day 13's night session this year, which will feature two Americans vying to become the first home favourite to win a Grand Slam in 23 years - Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe.

Shelton and Tiafoe have been scheduled second on men's semi-finals day despite Zverev having played his quarter-final on Wednesday rather than Tuesday with one eye on the demands of broadcasters' primetime slot

But the dip in prices throws into relief how important the game's biggest men's stars, Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner, have become to contemporary tennis.

While last season featured the young rivalry played out over three of the four Grand Slam finals, this year form and fitness has kept Alcaraz and Sinner from meeting in the biggest matches on tour.

Last year, both Alcaraz and Sinner played on Day 13, with the Spaniard beating the world No1 in their eventual final on Sunday. On host broadcaster ABC, their clash averaged 3million viewers, 82 per cent up on 2024.

This year, viewing figures have been more modest. The French Open, contested by Zverev and Flavio Cobolli, saw a 20-year viewing low, with just 1.3m viewers tuning in on broadcasters TNT and truTV.

Wimbledon viewers were also less tempted than 2025's Alcaraz-Sinner meeting one year on, with BBC registering a peak at 5.95million for the Italian's defeat of Zverev in four sets.

This was down on the previous year's 8.3million and the 7.5million who watched Alcaraz's second Wimbledon final against Novak Djokovic in 2024.

This US Open saw Sinner withdraw on the eve of the tournament as he continued to suffer from inflammation in his knee.

Alcaraz returned to competitive action in New York after four months nursing a wrist injury, but was knocked out in a five-set classic by Shelton - a quarter-final clash that would have sent viewership soaring through the roof, but for its early-hours finish at 3.34am on Wednesday morning.

Sports.title: Battle of boxing's most unlikeable stars: Conor Benn takes on troubled Ryan Garcia after burning Eddie Hearn with $10MILLION payday in his sights - but here's why Briton's fate rests solely in the hands of his narcissistic American rival
Sports.content:
Battle of boxing's most unlikeable stars: Conor Benn takes on troubled Ryan Garcia after burning Eddie Hearn with $10MILLION payday in his sights - but here's why Briton's fate rests solely in the hands of his narcissistic American rival

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

‘Who ya like buddy?’ It’s the most asked question in casino-ville as the hours tick down to this Saturday’s world title fight between two angry young men.

One, America’s extravagantly gifted but troubled world welterweight champion. The other, the ever-persistent English challenger who never stops throwing punches whether they connect or not. As if in manic obsession with defeating not only opponents but also his demons and a sceptical outside world.

So, Ryan Garcia or Conor Benn?

When the denizens of this neon gambling Strip in the Nevada desert ask that question they don’t’ want to know which of these two combatants you like personally more than the other. It is their way of trying to find out who you might be betting on to prevail in the atmospheric T-Mobile Arena.

Their inquiries are even more numerous than usual on such occasions as this. Because neither the Americans nor the Mexicans who are thronging here in support of their blood brother by heredity know very much about Benn. Other than the fact he is the son of a fabled icon of the British ring.

On his two previous US visits Benn Jr made hard work of beating men who looked more like nightclub bouncers than professional boxers. Of his exploits back home only the pair of fights against Chris Eubank Jr evoked any interest whatsoever on either side of this border.

What they are aware of is the two positive tests for performance enhancing drugs and the protracted legal battle to technically clear his name which kept him out of the ring for months. Just as they know about Garcia’s conviction and suspension for a similar finding.

Conor Benn is locked in the battle of boxing's most unlikeable stars in Las Vegas

Benn is lining up a $10m payday after burning his bridges with promoter Eddie Hearn

So, what’s to like?

There can be no doubting Benn’s work ethic. He trains like a dervish to manufacture the maximum possible out of however much natural-born ability he inherited from Nigel the Dark Destroyer. Nor does he ever give up. Eubank Jr had to go beyond the normal limits of even this battle-hardened business to inflict the only defeat of Conor’s career thus far. A loss he avenged, albeit in partly contrived and contentious circumstances.

Eubank the Younger was perilously drained in the rematch by a clause in the contract which prevented him rehydrating fully after struggling to cut poundage to meet the agreed catchweight.

What goes around comes around. If not in a full measure of the irony. Benn has had to sweat and strain down by almost a stone from middleweight to make the welterweight championship limit of 147 lbs. As he puts it: ‘Five weeks in hell.’

To say his body looks shredded is putting it mildly. But he has not been subjected to rehydration limitations following his Friday morning visit to the scales.

Eubank was handsomely rewarded to put his health on the line, and now Benn has been lured into similar jeopardy by the fortune – some reports say ten million dollars – he is receiving from UFC boss Dana White to be one of the first poster boys for his venture into boxing.

Benn tells it otherwise: ‘I’m doing this because I relish challenges. Have always wanted to strap on the same green WBC belt my dad was so proud to wear. To start getting the world titles that will leave a legacy for my kids. And to prove wrong everyone who doesn’t give me a chance of winning. That puts all the pressure on him, not me.’

Hearn backed the British fighter during his controversial doping ban saga

Ryan Garcia stands in his way of the WBC title, who is the more talented of the fighters

WEIGH-IN VERDICT: After all the brouhaha Conor Benn made the weight with a full pound to spare After what he described as 'five weeks of hell' dieting down by two divisions he scaled 146 lbs in readiness to challenge world welterweight champion Ryan Garcia here this Saturday night. He did so with a told-you so smile. Throughout the speculation as to whether he could shed the best part of a stone in his training camp journey from middleweight Benn had assured one and all that he would be comfortable at his long-ago weight. Good as his word he came in only half a pound heavier than Garcia. Although he is leaner of hip the muscle is still there on arms and torso. Complete with a six pack as a reminder of his constant work ethic. The slightly taller part/Mexican great white hope of American boxing does look more natural at the weight. But Benn does not appear stressed from all his exertions. Even so Garcia is still a solid odds on favourite in the Vegas betting

Whether or not Benn can take in sufficient liquids and pasta before entering the ring, the dangers to him are greater than those with which Eubank struggled. Garcia, one year the younger at 28 but the riper in championships experience, has authentic one-hit-knockout power.

Benn goes into his first world championship fight reliant on the cumulative effect of his non-stop output. The problem with this is that King Ry is probably the best counterpuncher in the world right now and Benn’s headlong style will likely suit him nicely, thank you.

To complicate the evaluation, both have blotted their copybooks as people. Garcia, the handsome heartthrob, burnished his bad-boy rock-star image by trashing a five-star hotel room. He also needed his family’s help with overcoming mental problems aggravated by a passing fancy for social drugs and booze.

Benn invited mockery for claiming initially that he failed his drugs tests because of eating enough eggs to fill the shelves of all the Tescos in London. Then, in order to collect his bonanza from Mister UFC, he unceremoniously dumped his long-time promoter Eddie Hearn who had bankrolled his hefty legal costs and loaned him half a million quid to help sustain his flamboyant lifestyle through that crisis.

Not much to like there.

So, when it comes to the fight, who ya like? The answer is not Conor Benn’s to give. Because the real question is which Ryan Garcia turns up.

If it is the narcissist whose arrogant complacency has cost him a couple of big fights, it may not be totally beyond the bounds of possibility that Conor could pull off one of the major upsets by a British boxer abroad.

If it is King Ry fully prepared and ready to unfurl all the majesty then we can only hope the son of Nigel is not seriously hurt.

Sports.title: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan quietly inks new contract after team's scandalized offseason
Sports.content:
Kyle Shanahan didn’t just pick up a win during the San Francisco 49ers’ recent road trip to Melbourne, Australia. The 10th-year head coach also got himself a contract extension at a particularly welcome moment for the team.

According to multiple reports, the 46-year-old son of two-time Super Bowl-winning head coach Mike Shanahan has received a multiyear extension with the Niners. Terms of the deal were not immediately released.

The Daily Mail has sought comment from team officials.

Shanahan has gone 83-67 over his decade by the Bay. Over that time, the 49ers have reached the playoffs six times, including two trips to the Super Bowl, both of which ended in defeat.

The 49ers picked up a surprisingly easy 27-7 Week 1 win over the rival Los Angeles Rams – a team considered by many to be a Super Bowl contender. The victory was a welcome change for a team that has been decimated by injuries, including Shanahan’s own absence from training camp after a serious offseason car crash.

The July 14 incident had been shrouded in mystery after Palo Alto police initially refused to release an accident report or bodycam footage while officers initially blamed the other driver only for Shanahan to ultimately take responsibility.

Kyle Shanahan has reportedly received a new contract extension with the 49ers

Niners fans had reason to celebrate on Thursday night as San Francisco tormented LA

Later it was revealed that Shanahan collided with a car driven by a 21-year-old woman, saying the crash occurred when he reached for his phone.

The incident left Shanahan with a concussion, broken ribs, a broken nose, a broken hand and more than 40 stitches to close a cut over his eye. A few symptoms from the concussion remain.

As he told reporters at training camp, Shanahan was driving at around 20mph with his Tesla in autopilot mode when the crash happened. In autopilot mode, Tesla 'matches the speed of your vehicle to that of the surrounding traffic' and 'assists in steering within a clearly marked lane, and uses traffic-aware cruise control.'

But Shanahan insisted he still should not have taken his eyes off the road when he reached behind his seat for his phone.

'I've had autopilot for nine years, so I'm pretty comfortable with it,' he said. 'Who knows what happened when I turned around, whether it malfunctioned or whether I knocked it off. That's something that I don't know yet.

'But regardless, that is always your fault, whether you're in autopilot or not. You can't take your eyes off the road. It's a partnership driving.

The 49ers' offseason was marred by Jeff York's arrest and guilty plea for disorderly conduct

'You don't just turn it over to a computer. It's a good lesson, no matter how comfortable I am with that, that I believe someday could save my life or someone else's.'

Shanahan was the only person who needed to be hospitalized and police didn't issue him a ticket for the cell phone use.

And of course, the car crash was the least of the 49ers worries after top executive Jed York was arrested after allegedly trying to pay $140 for sex at an Ohio trailer park. The 46-year-old pleaded no contest to charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools. He was sentenced to one day in jail and fined $1,150.

For his part, Shanahan has tried to claim that York's arrest is 'irrelevant' to his players, while linebacker Fred Warner insisted it wasn't a topic of conversation in the locker room.

Sports.title: Ranked: World football's most-expensively assembled squads - with £1.05bn Liverpool flops taking top spot and Tottenham outspending PSG and Real Madrid... so where is YOUR club in the ultimate rich list?
Sports.content:
The big-spending superpowers of world football splashed the cash to record levels this summer, but who has the most expensive squad?

Once known for their shrewd, under-the-radar dealings in the transfer market and eye for a bargain, Liverpool have changed their approach now, opting for the best players money can buy rather than filling out squad depth.

And that's reflected in the CIES Football Observatory stats boffins' rankings, with the Reds in top spot.

Liverpool's squad spend has now reached a whopping £1.05billion and moves them up three places compared to last year, topping the table that Chelsea had led a season ago.

The eye-catching signing of Bradley Barcola for £123million from PSG was the major outlay in the summer transfer window, supplemented by deals for Victor Munoz (£35m) and young Genk goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans (£30m). .

Combined with last year's major deals for Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak, who are both yet to fully find their feet at Anfield, it is eye-watering expenditure.

Florian Wirtz (left) and Alexander Isak (right) are part of the most expensive squad in football

While Liverpool are top of the tree in terms of squad cost, other Premier League sides also make up the top six.

It's hardly a surprise given the English top flight shattered the spending record by buying £3.56billion-worth of talent during the window.

In second spot is Manchester City, who have a squad value of marginally less than Andoni Iraola's side at £1.04billion.

Tottenham's major moves in the transfer market have seen them move up to third.

Spurs spent £320m on seven new players. Savio joined for £85m, Omar Marmoush has a £65m option, Mateus Fernandes was £85m, and Sandro Tonali a whopping £100m from Newcastle in addition to £52m for Jan Paul van Hecke.

Behind them are Chelsea, who fall three places from last year, while Manchester United and champions Arsenal are fifth and sixth respectively.

United spent £163m on new additions this summer, a relatively modest sum in comparison to years gone by, while the Gunners were unable to secure the big-money attacking player they craved.

Arsenal still managed to cough up £194m in total on the likes of Ezri Konsa, Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis.

Sports.title: Richarlison's move to Brazil COLLAPSES: Spurs star fails to agree terms with Vasco da Gama as Roberto De Zerbi issues cryptic response to threat of legal action amid contract row
Sports.content:
Richarlison's move to Brazil COLLAPSES: Spurs star fails to agree terms with Vasco da Gama as Roberto De Zerbi issues cryptic response to threat of legal action amid contract row

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Roberto De Zerbi insists there are no regrets at Tottenham about the handling of Richarlison's future - with the forward rejecting the chance to move to Vasco da Gama in Brazil, according to reports in the country.

The Brazilian was left out of De Zerbi's squad after rejecting a move to Everton before the transfer deadline, which caused a move for Iliman Ndiaye to fall through.

One of his final hopes of getting out of the north London club was a move to his homeland, but it is reported that there is no agreement on personal terms, despite expectations from Vasco that Tottenham would be open to a deal.

It is understood a three-and-a-half-year deal was on offer for the 29-year-old, but that he is not currently looking to move back to Brazil.

After the Ndiaye deal fell through, Spurs turned instead to sign Mykhailo Mudryk who was injured in training this week and out for up to two months.

'I am sorry because I have one player less on the list,' said De Zerbi. 'Richarlison is a good guy. I spoke with him a lot and spent time trying to convince him to stay.

Roberto De Zerbi (left) has responded to Richarlison's (centre) threat of legal action against Tottenham

'But I know the truth. I know what happened in the last month, the last 45 days and I know the behaviour of Richarlison. And it's clear.

'I can't explain it because it's not right but I'm sorry because it could have been different and in a different way it could have been better.'

Richarlison, top scorer last season for Spurs with 11 Premier League goals, has been exploring legal action to have the final nine months of his contract nullified amid interest from Brazil.

Spurs have not scored in their first three games of the season and did not have a shot on target in the goalless draw at Nottingham Forest last week.

De Zerbi is certain there are enough goals in his team however and challenged Omar Marmoush to shoulder more of the burden.

'Marmoush is playing well,' said the Spurs boss. 'In Nottingham he played a good game, not a fantastic game, not fantastic with the last decision. But he was alive and in the game. He seemed to be dangerous.

'He is smart, understands football. In terms of goals, he is not Harry Kane but he can score more goals than he has done in the last two seasons.

'About Manchester City, I don't want to speak because not my experience but at Eintracht Frankfurt he scored lots of goals. If you analyse his qualities he can score more goals and has to demand more goals of himself.'

De Zerbi could look to pair Marmoush with Dominic Solanke in the search for the right chemistry in attack. 'They can play together,' he said. 'When we signed Marmoush we thought he could play with another striker or alone.'

Sports.title: Former Premier League footballer Nathaniel Mendez-Laing, 34, charged with beating his wife as he appears in court
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League winger Nathaniel Mendez-Laing has appeared in court after being charged with beating his wife.

The 34-year-old, who currently plays for MK Dons, was accused of assaulting his spouse, Saira Mendez-Laing back in June at their Staffordshire home.

He was arrested after police were called to the property in Shenstone and charged with assault by beating. The Crown Prosecution Service then authorised those charges last month.

Mendez-Laing appeared in Cannock magistrates' court on Friday and denied the charge.

Mendez-Laing and Saira, who is the mother of his child, have only been married for a year having tied the knot last summer.

He was seen entering the court on crutches and confirmed his name, age and address, without speaking further.

Nathaniel Mendez-Laing, pictured with his wife Saira, denies the charge of beating her

The court heard that Mendez-Laing was accused of hitting his wife over the head repeatedly and injuring her arm in the alleged incident.

The dispute between the couple started over a 'disagreement about a phone', but the footballer insists the confrontation did not turn into a physical assault.

The case will go to trial in January next year and the judge, Joseph O'Connor, allowed Mendez-Laing conditional bail rather than remanding him in custody.

MK Dons have said they cannot comment on an ongoing case and are struggling in League One this season.

Mendez-Laing played in the Premier League for Cardiff in 2019-20 and scored four times in 20 games for the Welsh side.

He also turns out for Guatemala, who he qualifies for through his mother and maternal grandmother.

Mendez-Laing has not been seen on the pitch since the opening day of the League One campaign. He moved to MK Dons after spending three years at Derby, during which time he scored 19 goals in 131 games.

Sports.title: Aston Villa complain to refs chiefs about new rule change as they join Premier League clubs to raise concerns
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have raised concerns with referees' chiefs about new rules regarding injuries and substitutions. Any player who receives medical attention on the pitch must leave it and remain on the touchline for 60 seconds, meaning their team is reduced to ten for that period. And if a player takes more than ten seconds to leave the field after being substituted, his replacement is not allowed to enter the field until the first break in play after a minute has elapsed. Daily Mail Sport understands Villa are not the only Premier League club to raise concerns with refereeing body Pro Ref this term. The feeling among these clubs is that referees are not using sufficient judgment to determine when a player is genuinely injured and when he is wasting time. Unai Emery's men are looking for their first Premier League win and goal of the season after they got off the mark in the Champions League at Club Brugge in the week. One of the club's most eye-catching signings this summer was Alejandro Garnacho, who joined on an initial loan deal from Chelsea – days after Morgan Rogers moved in the opposite direction for £117million. Aston Villa have joined other Premier League clubs in complaining about new rules around injuries and substitutions Garnacho has struggled to rediscover the level of his early days at Manchester United and Emery needs to see more from the 22-year-old, who has played for only 31 minutes until now. Emery said: 'His attitude is positive. Now he needs time and hard work every day and he is showing it. It's most important to be consistent and demanding through his attitude, and then eventually he will achieve his best level.'

Sports.title: West Ham footballer Edson Alvarez forced to deny bombshell claims linking him to a KIDNAPPING plot
Sports.content:
West Ham footballer Edson Alvarez forced to deny bombshell claims linking him to a KIDNAPPING plot

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

West Ham midfielder Edson Alvarez says he 'categorically rejects' allegations linking him to an alleged kidnapping plot.

Mexican film-maker Juan Jose Lopez Ordonez had publicly made the allegations earlier this week in an interview with TVNotas.

Ordonez claimed he was kidnapped in November 2024, with two people forcing their way into his car before blindfolding him and threatening him with weapons.

He stated that his attackers had also inserted a syringe into his neck, with his kidnappers claiming they were acting under orders from Alvarez's then father-in-law Jonathan Toache Bedolla.

Ordonez said bystanders had helped him to escape and that he reported the incident to the police.

He claimed Alvarez was not directly involved in his kidnapping but was aware of the plot.

West Ham midfielder Edson Alvarez says he 'categorically rejects' allegations he was involved in an alleged kidnapping plot

The film-maker alleged he is owed 3.5million pesos (£152,000) by Alvarez following working on a documentary about the Mexico captain, which was claimed to have been produced ahead of the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

Ordonez said he asked for payment in 2024 and alleged he was also involved in a dispute with Alvarez's father-in-law over a property he owned at the time.

He claimed Alvarez's then father-in-law paid to have the investigation stopped.

Alvarez has posted a lengthy response on social media to deny Ordonez's claims and has vowed to take legal action against the 'false allegations'.

'In light of the publications and statements that have circulated recently, I believe it is necessary to address this matter clearly and firmly,' Alvarez wrote.

'I categorically reject any allegation or attempt to associate my name with events, conflicts, or conduct that are entirely unrelated to me.

'Over the past several months, my name and image have repeatedly been used to generate greater media attention around a situation that has nothing to do with me.

'Until now, I had chosen not to respond. However, there are limits, and attributing knowledge, responsibility, or involvement in matters of this nature to me without presenting a single piece of evidence clearly crosses that line.

'If anyone believes they have evidence of any wrongdoing on my part, there are authorities, prosecutors, and courts before which they can present it.

Alvarez released a statement on Instagram to deny claims made by Mexican filmmaker Juan Jose Lopez Ordonez in an interview this week

'Serious accusations must be supported by evidence and presented before the appropriate authorities, not through statements in media outlets whose content prioritizes sensationalism and media exposure over accuracy and truth.

'I will not allow my name to be used to fuel conflicts between third parties or to gain media exposure. Therefore, given the seriousness of the statements that have been made, I have instructed my legal team to evaluate and pursue the appropriate legal action against any person who makes or disseminates false allegations against me.

'I also want to be clear regarding the publications that have attempted to connect me to this matter through my former partner's father: It is not my place to confirm, deny, or comment on what may be said about third parties, but it is my responsibility to make one thing absolutely clear: I have nothing to do with the events being reported.

'Throughout nearly ten years of my professional career, I have made every effort to stay away from media scandals and to have my name recognized for my work both on and off the pitch. I come from a hardworking and honorable family that taught me that a reputation is built over many years through hard work, discipline, and conduct. For that very reason, I will not allow mine to be irresponsibly used to involve me in matters that are entirely unrelated to me.

'My priority is, and will continue to be, where it has always been: my daughters, my family, and my professional career.'

Alvarez, who has made 102 appearances for Mexico, captained his national team at this summer's World Cup.

The 28-year-old was expected to leave West Ham in the transfer window but failed to seal a move.

Alvarez has made 74 appearances for the Hammers since joining from Ajax in 2023.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
