NEW DELHI: Supreme Court has directed FSSAI to spell out details of how front-of-pack food warning labels will look, their shape, size, colour, placement on packets and the timeline of implementation, leaving nothing to the discretion of the food regulator.The court also wanted to know how Centre plans to warn children about the dangers of junk food.After FSSAI agreed to implement labelling after being pushed by SC and filed an affidavit, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran put 13 questions to the regulator and gave 10 days' time for answers.Though SC acknowledged "significant progress" has been made by FSSAI on this issue of national importance, it said the regulator's affidavit was silent on various issues and several aspects of practical implementation required clarification.The 13 questions are part of the detailed order uploaded by the court on Friday, which also includes its observations from the previous day on why FSSAI proposed a two-phase rollout of the labelling requirements instead of implementing them in one go.According to FSSAIâs proposal, during Phase I, a red hexagonal warning would be placed on products high in two or more nutrients of concern, namely added fat, added sugar and salt, based on thresholds in the Dietary Guidelines for Indians, 2024.The warning could carry declarations such as âHIGH FATâ, âHIGH SUGARâ, âHIGH SALTâ and âHIGHLY SWEETENED BEVERAGEâ. The proposed Phase II would extend the warning to products high in any one of the specified nutrients. The order questions the regulator on what basis it suggested the inclusion of food products high in âtwo or moreâ nutrients of concern and certain sweetened beverages in Phase I, and the inclusion of food products high in âany oneâ nutrient of concern in Phase II, respectively.The court also said sugar, salt and fat are called the âUnholy Trinityâ and that âthe âunholinessâ arises not only from the added sugar and added fat in a food product but the total value of these nutrients available in a product, which has to be considered.â The Supreme Court incorporated the suggestion of advocate Rajiv Shankar Dvivedi that the threshold must be decided based on âtotal sugarâ and âtotal fatâ and not on the basis of âadded sugarâ and âadded fatâ. Referring to the 2021 FSSAI meeting, the Bench said, âIt is clear from the aforesaid minutes that âtotal sugarâ and âsaturated fatâ would be used for the purpose of the labelling. In this regard, we would like FSSAI to weigh in and indicate whether there has been a change in stance in comparison to the consensus arrived at in the aforesaid stakeholder consultation. If so, we would like to know how the underlying concerns are sought to be addressed.âThe court also asked the regulator: âWhat are the dimensions of the âred hexagonâ proposed to be used in the FoPL (labelling)? Whether it would have standardised specifications or whether it would be calculated in proportion to the area of the package? Whether the font size used for FoPL would be relative to the dimensions of the hexagon themselves? The manner and method of the placement of such hexagon(s)?â It further asked, âWhy has FSSAI suggested a combined/composite/singular hexagon for two or more nutrients of concern instead of separate/distinct/individual hexagons for each nutrient of concern?â The court posted the matter for hearing on September 28.

World.title: India to present 37 deep-tech ventures at Brics forum
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A cervical cancer screening system that assesses risks in under 60 seconds and an electric motor that does away with rare-earth materials will be among Indian innovations showcased to Brics leaders this week.

Thirty-seven deep-tech ventures are participating in the two-day Brics Bharat Innovates Exposition. Among them is Periwinkle Technologies' AI-enabled cervical cancer screening and triage platform, which provides a risk assessment in under a minute. Janitri Innovations is bringing an AI system that monitors mothers and foetuses for clinical risks, while Niramai has developed radiation-free thermal imaging for early breast cancer screening.

Chara Technologies will showcase rare-earth-free electric powertrains. QpiAI's quantum computing systems ra-nge from an eight-qubit machine for education and research to its 64-qubit Kaveri processor.

Space technologies include Dhruva Space's small-satellite platforms and GalaxEye's Drishti, which combines radar and optical sensors to produce all-weather earth imagery. Other innovations tackle industrial problems: AI-based fruit grading, robotic warehouse sorting, real-time earthquake warning, pipeline inspection and carbon capture.

World.title: Russia & Iran hit out at US 'aggression', pose a challenge for summit host India
World.content:

New Delhi: Russia and Iran Friday hit out at US and other Western powers for imposing sanctions and "acts of aggression", and called upon Brics to work on strategies that make the group more resilient to deal with challenges and pressures, in what underlined the challenge India faces in seeking to stop the meeting from turning into an anti-West platform."Iran has faced extensive sanctions over the past years. However, in recent months, these pressures have entered a far more dangerous phase as a result of the military act of aggression of US and the Israelis against Iran. This... in addition to material losses, once again revealed an important reality: economic security cannot be separated from national and regional security," Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said at Brics Business Forum."Whenever the trade energy infrastructure or the financial system of a country comes under political or military pressure, its effects extend beyond the country's borders and can affect regional or even global stability," he said.Russian President Vladimir Putin hit out at the "old leaders" resorting to "every conceivable means to reclaim their erstwhile dominance".He said, "They go so far as to employ instruments of direct physical force, including the destruction of industrial and logistical infrastructure...Efforts are under way to block international transport corridors, to seize sea-going vessels, while illegal restrictions are imposed, accompanied by threats of so-called secondary sanctions, on those who refuse to act in the interests of others and instead seek to defend their own national interests. "The speeches offered a glimpse into the task awaiting India, which will be called upon to reconcile the hostility with its own policy of flexible multi-alignment. India is aware that the Trump administration will be keeping a close watch on the Brics deliberations because of Russia and Iran's anger over sanctions and China's interest in pushing for moves such as de-dollarisation and a cross-border payment system that can rival West-controlled SWIFT. US President Donald Trump has made no bones of his opposition to Brics.Putin sought investment platforms to fund projects in trade, infrastructure and technology. "We are ready to contribute to the world's energy and food security with our partners, and to jointly shape reliable global routes, such as Trans-Arctic Transport Corridor and North-South International Corridor," he said.Pezeshkian said, "Food and energy security are two fundamental pillars of economic security, and Iran, with its vast energy reserves and outstanding geographical position, is prepared to play the role of a strategic partner in Brics food, energy and transport supply chains."He batted for expanding tr-ade in local currency, building a reinsurance pool with a $10 billion initial corpus, and fina-ncing infrastructure through New Development Bank. Putin, too, backed NDB and sought leveraging it to create a new investment platform.

World.title: Goyal: Pull down barriers, allow easy movement to professionals
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Commerce and industry minister

Friday called for dismantling of trade barriers by Brics nations while urging them to link payment systems and trade in each other's local currency.

"We should open our markets for each other's products, including raw material and critical minerals. Our supply chains will be resilient when they run both ways, with non-tariff measures imposing higher import costs, in fact much more than the tariffs themselves," the minister said at Brics Business Forum.

He called for streamlining regulatory and customs processes while also promoting services trade. "Let us open our services market for each other in the real sense, let professionals move easily across borders and make it easier to recognise each other's professional qualifications," the minister said.

The comments come amid several countries holding up visas for Indian professionals and some like China mounting curbs on the export of many items while denying market access to goods from parts of the world.

Pointing to initiatives taken by govt in laying out digital public infrastructure, Goyal said, "Today, it (UPI) is also accepted in 11 countries and I would urge Brics member countries and partner countries to link our payment systems, trade in each other's local currencies, make digital trade global and build together for the future emerging technologies."

External affairs minister S Jaishankar called upon member nations to work towards addressing economic challenges by ensuring transparent trade and investment practices. "The common thread is how to make it easier for businesses in our countries to find more partners, access more markets, connect supply networks and convert complementarities into viable commercial partnerships," the EAM said, while pointing to geopolitical tensions.

World.title: Counting Discounts
World.content:
How good is that online deal? Weâll know from Jan 1

For years, UK consumer group âWhich?â has found that many Black Friday deals are not really bargains. A shop may say a product has been cut from Â£500 to Â£400, but the product may never have actually sold for Â£500.

Last year, none of the deals checked by the group was the cheapest price that product had been sold for in the previous 12 months.

You may have seen something similar during festive sales in India. A product you have been waiting to buy during a Diwali sale may suddenly become more expensive when the sale begins. The âdiscountedâ price may even be the same as, or higher than, its earlier price.

The good news is that this should change on e-commerce platforms in India from January 1.

Under new rules, when a seller announces a discount, it will also have to show the productâs âprior priceâ. This means the lowest price at which the product was sold on that platform during the 30 days before the discount was announced.

This gives shoppers a simple way to check whether a discount is real. Without such a rule, it is easy to be fooled when big sale signs and huge discounts create excitement.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Other major markets already have similar protections. In the US, the Federal Trade Commission says a âformer priceâ used in an  must be a genuine price.





California says it must have been the normal market price within the previous 90 days. The European Union introduced a similar rule in 2022, using a 30-day price history. Its rule also applies to shops, not just online sellers.

India should do the same. Online shoppers can use price-tracking websites to check whether a deal is genuine. But if a shop puts a â60% offâ sign on a shirt, there is no easy way to know whether it was really sold at the higher price before. A discount should be a real saving, not just a clever trick.

World.title: 40% of global GDP is here: PM Modi
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Noting that the Brics grouping now represents 50% of the global population, 40% of GDP, and 25% of trade, PM Narendra Modi said Friday that their collective economic might has grown at nearly double the global pace since the bloc was formed in 2006, and called upon member countries to reduce barriers to trade and increase opportunities for businesses.

In his address at the Brics Business Forum, PM also underlined the need to keep trade flowing. "Global trade can move forward only when sea lanes are secure, supply routes are open, and seafarers are safe. And, therefore, Bharat is a firm supporter of freedom of navigation and the safety of seafarers," Modi said, his remark coming against the backdrop of disruption of traffic through Strait of Hormuz and the growing threat through Bab al-Mandab Strait, another crucial artery for India.

His pitch for deeper engagement significantly contrasted the themes of 2 other key members: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.

Putin, like PM, also invoked the growing economic heft of Brics members. However, he and Pezeshkian, with their countries reeling from sanctions, were resentful of the West's continuing sway.

"The world is changing... Over the past 5 years, as it has been said today - I think it was our Indonesian colleague who said it, the Brics countries accounted for over 40% of global GDP, while the contribution of Group of Seven, the so-called leading economies, although I don't understand why they are called 'leading', was just 29%," Putin said.





PM Modi

's 'Intra-Brics trade' call seen as aimed at US and China

At a time when trade barriers are increasing, India is building economic bridges, PM Narendra Modi said, adding, âOur approach in Brics is also the same: to reduce barriers and increase opportunities for businesses.â

He has been averse to Brics being turned into an anti-West bloc and has resisted the push from China, Russia and Iran for de-dollarisation. Also, his call for greater intra-Brics commerce can be seen as aimed at both US President Trumpâs strong arm tariff tactics as well as a reminder of New Delhiâs contention to China that it needed to let in more Indian goods and should not weaponise supplies of equipment and raw materials needed by Indian manufacturers.

âIn these years, the combined GDP of Brics countries has grown by about 4.5 times while the global GDP has grown by around 2.5 times. Bricsâs economic strength has grown at nearly double the pace of the world,â Modi said, pointing to the bloc comprising emerging markets and developing economies.

He called upon the Brics Business Council to identify the top 10 trade barriers to be removed, while charting the growth trajectory of the Indian economy in the last 12 years since his govt took office with its focus on innovation and resilience.

âCan we support 100 Brics startups every year to scale in other Brics markets? Can we develop 1,000 new partnerships among our businesses? On all these benchmarks, we have to review our progress every year. Let us turn the ambition of Brics into action and its collective strength into global solutions. Let Brics move forward and take the world forward as well.â

Lauding Brics nations for becoming key centres for global innovation and solutions â from grassroots to frontier tech â he said the blocâs growing scale, speed, and optimism are clearly visible.

With the theme of Indiaâs Brics presidency being âBuilding for Resilience, Innovation, Co-operation and Sustainabilityâ, he said India has made this foundation of its economic and trade policy.

India has made supply chains from energy to technology more diversified and reliable, he said, adding that it is offering confidence in growth and stability even amid global uncertainties.
